bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑巻第二百一十四

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十】起閼逢閹茂，盡重光大荒落，凡八年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 30] From jianmao through dahuoluo; eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 30] From the jianmao year through dahuoluo—eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己巳，上-{發}-西京；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jisi, the Emperor departed the Western Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jisi, the Emperor set out from Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 己-{丑}-，至東都。

translations.literal: On jichou, he arrived at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 張九齡自韶州入見，求終喪；

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling came from Shaozhou to have an audience and requested to complete his mourning period;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling came up from Shaozhou for an audience and asked to be allowed to finish his mourning obligations;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅，秦州地連震，壞公私屋殆盡，吏民壓死者四千-{餘}-人；

translations.literal: In the second month, on renyin, Qinzhou suffered successive earthquakes; public and private buildings were nearly all destroyed, and more than four thousand officials and commoners were crushed to death;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renyin, a series of earthquakes struck Qinzhou, destroying almost all public and private buildings and killing more than four thousand officials and civilians;

sentences.zh: 命左丞相蕭-{嵩}-賑恤。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Left Chancellor Xiao Song to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Left Chancellor Xiao Song to organize relief and aid.

sentences.zh: 方士張果自言有神仙-{術}-，誑人-{云}-堯時爲侍中，-{於}-今數千歳；

translations.literal: The Daoist adept Zhang Guo claimed to possess immortal arts and deceived people, saying that in the time of Yao he had been a palace attendant and that he was now several thousand years old;
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist adept Zhang Guo claimed supernatural powers and told people he had served as a palace attendant in the age of Yao and was now several thousand years old;

sentences.zh: 多往來恆山中，則天以來，屢-{-{征}-}-不至。

translations.literal: He often traveled about Mount Heng; since the reign of Empress Wu he had repeatedly been summoned but never came.
translations.idiomatic: He frequented Mount Heng, and since Empress Wu's time had been summoned many times but never appeared at court.

sentences.zh: 恆州刺史韋濟-{薦}-之，上遣中書-{舍}-人徐嶠繼璽書迎之。

translations.literal: The prefect of Hengzhou, Wei Ji, recommended him, and the Emperor sent Palace Attendant Xu Qiao with successive imperial letters to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou prefect Wei Ji recommended him, and the Emperor sent Secretariat Drafter Xu Qiao with repeated imperial summons to escort him to court.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，至東都，肩輿入宮，恩禮甚厚。

translations.literal: On gengyin he arrived at the Eastern Capital, was carried into the palace in a sedan chair, and received very generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he reached Luoyang, was borne into the palace in a sedan chair, and was treated with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 張九齡請不禁鑄錢，三月，庚辰，敕百官議之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling requested that the ban on private coinage not be lifted; in the third month, on gengchen, an edict ordered the hundred officials to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling had urged against lifting the ban on private coinage; in the third month, on gengchen, the Emperor ordered the court to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿等皆曰：「一啓此門，恐小人棄農逐利，而濫惡更甚。

translations.literal: Pei Yaoji and others all said: "Once this door is opened, I fear petty men will abandon farming to pursue profit, and debased coin will grow worse still.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoji and others argued: "Once that gate is opened, petty men will abandon farming for profit, and debased coin will only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 」秘書監崔沔曰：「若稅銅折役，則官冶可成，計估度庸，則私鑄無利，易而可久，簡而難誣。

translations.literal: Secretary Supervisor Cui Hao said: "If copper is taxed and corvée commuted, then official minting can succeed; if levies are assessed by estimated corvée value, then private casting will be unprofitable—easy to sustain and hard to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: " Director of the Palace Library Cui Hao said: "Tax copper and commute labor service, and official minting can work; assess levies by estimated corvée value, and private casting will not pay—simple, durable, and hard to cheat.

sentences.zh: 且夫錢之爲物，貴以通貨，利不在多，何待私鑄然-{後}-足用也！

translations.literal: Moreover, as for money as a commodity, its value lies in circulating goods; the benefit is not in quantity—why must we wait for private casting before there is enough for use!
translations.idiomatic: Money exists to circulate goods; the point is not sheer volume—why must we rely on private casting before the supply is adequate?

sentences.zh: 」右監門録事參軍劉秩曰：「夫人富則不可以賞勸，貧則不可以威禁，若許其私鑄，貧者必不能爲之；

translations.literal: " Right Gatekeeper Record Officer Liu Zhi said: "When people are rich they cannot be encouraged by rewards; when poor they cannot be restrained by punishments. If private casting is permitted, the poor certainly cannot do it;
translations.idiomatic: " Right Gatekeeper Record Officer Liu Zhi said: "The rich cannot be moved by rewards alone, nor the poor restrained by punishments alone. If private casting is allowed, the poor will never be able to do it;

sentences.zh: 臣恐貧者益貧而役-{於}-富，富者益富而逞其欲。

translations.literal: your servant fears the poor will grow poorer while serving the rich, and the rich will grow richer while indulging their desires.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the poor will only grow poorer in service to the rich, while the rich grow richer and indulge every appetite.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝時，呉王濞富埒天子，鑄錢所致也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, King Liu Pi of Wu was as wealthy as the Son of Heaven—this came from casting coin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Han, King Liu Pi of Wu grew as wealthy as the emperor himself—because he cast his own coin.

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 秩，子玄之子也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi was the son of Liu Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi was a son of Liu Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬辰，以朔方節度使信安王禕兼關内道採訪處置使，增領涇、原等十二州。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renchen, Prince Xin'an Li Yi, military commissioner of Shuofang, was also made investigation and disposition commissioner of Guannei Circuit, with twelve additional prefectures including Jing and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renchen, Prince Xin'an Li Yi, commissioner of Shuofang, was also appointed investigation and disposition commissioner for Guannei Circuit, gaining authority over twelve additional prefectures including Jing and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎李林甫，柔佞多狡數，深結宦官及妃嬪家，侍候上動靜，無不知之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Li Linfu was supple, fawning, and full of crafty schemes; he formed deep ties with eunuchs and the households of imperial consorts, attending to the Emperor's movements until nothing escaped his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Li Linfu was smooth, fawning, and endlessly cunning; he cultivated eunuchs and consorts' kin and watched the Emperor's every move until nothing escaped him.

sentences.zh: 由是毎奏對，常稱旨，上悅之。

translations.literal: Because of this, whenever he presented memorials or answered at audience he usually matched the Emperor's intent, and the Emperor was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he memorialized or answered at audience he usually hit the mark, and the Emperor took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 時武惠妃寵幸傾-{後}-宮，生壽王淸，諸子莫得爲比，太子浸疎薄。

translations.literal: At that time Consort Wu Huifei enjoyed favor that overshadowed the rear palace; she bore Prince Shou Li Qing, and none of the other princes could compare— the Crown Prince was gradually treated with growing distance.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu Huifei then enjoyed favor that eclipsed the entire inner palace; she had borne Prince Shou Li Qing, and no other prince could rival him—the Crown Prince was steadily pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 林甫乃因宦官言-{於}-惠妃，-{願}-盡力保護壽王；

translations.literal: Linfu thereupon spoke through eunuchs to Huifei, expressing his wish to do his utmost to protect Prince Shou;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu then spoke to Huifei through eunuchs, pledging to do everything in his power to protect Prince Shou;

sentences.zh: 惠妃德之，陰爲内助，由是擢黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Huifei was grateful to him and secretly aided him within; because of this he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huifei was grateful and quietly backed him from within, and he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊子，以裴耀卿爲侍中，張九齡爲中書令，林甫爲禮部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Pei Yaoji was made Palace Attendant, Zhang Jiuling Grand Councilor of the Secretariat, and Linfu Minister of Rites with concurrent status as Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Pei Yaoji was appointed Palace Attendant, Zhang Jiuling Grand Councilor, and Linfu Minister of Rites with concurrent status as Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 上-{種}-麥-{於}-苑中，帥太子以來親往芟之，謂曰：「此所以-{薦}-宗廟，故不敢不親，且欲使汝曹知稼穡艱難耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor planted wheat in the imperial park, led the Crown Prince and the others to go in person to reap it, and said to them: "This is what is offered to the ancestral temple, so I dare not fail to do it myself, and I also wish to let you know how hard farming is.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor planted wheat in the imperial park, brought the Crown Prince and his brothers to reap it in person, and told them: "This grain is for the ancestral temple, so I dare not leave the work to others—and I want you to understand how hard farming truly is.

sentences.zh: 」又遍以賜侍臣曰：「比遣人視田中稼，多不得實，故自-{種}-以觀之。

translations.literal: " He also distributed it widely to attending ministers, saying: "Lately when I sent men to inspect the crops in the fields, they often did not report the truth, so I planted it myself to observe.
translations.idiomatic: " He also shared the harvest with his attending ministers, saying: "When I lately sent men to inspect the crops, their reports were often false, so I planted this myself to see the truth.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬辰，幽州節度使張守珪大破契丹，遣使獻捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renchen, Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of Youzhou, inflicted a great defeat on the Khitan and sent envoys to present news of victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen, Youzhou commissioner Zhang Shougui routed the Khitan and sent envoys to report his victory.

sentences.zh: 薛王業疾病，上憂之，容-{發}-爲變。

translations.literal: Prince Xue Li Ye fell ill; the Emperor was anxious for him, and his countenance changed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xue Li Ye fell gravely ill; the Emperor was deeply worried, and his face showed it.

sentences.zh: 七月，己巳，薨，贈謚惠宣太子。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on jisi, he died; posthumously he was given the title Prince Hui Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on jisi, he died and was posthumously honored as Prince Hui Xuan.

sentences.zh: 上以裴耀卿爲江淮、河南轉運使，-{於}-河口置輸塲。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Pei Yaoji transport commissioner for the Jiang-Huai and Henan regions and established a transshipment depot at the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Pei Yaoji transport commissioner for the Jiang-Huai and Henan regions and established a transshipment depot at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，-{於}-輸塲東置河陰倉，西置柏崖倉，三門東置集津倉，西置鹽倉；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin, east of the transshipment depot he established Heyin Granary, west of it Baiya Granary, east of Sanmen Pass Jijin Granary, and west of it Yan Granary;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin, east of the depot he built Heyin Granary and west of it Baiya Granary; east of Sanmen Pass he built Jijin Granary and west of it Yan Granary;

sentences.zh: 鑿漕渠十八-{里}-，以避三門之險。

translations.literal: he excavated an eighteen-li canal transport channel to avoid the perils of Sanmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: and he cut an eighteen-li canal to bypass the hazards of Sanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 先是，舟運江、淮之米至東都含嘉倉，僦車陸運，三百-{里}-至陝，率兩斛用十錢。

translations.literal: Previously, grain from the Jiang and Huai was shipped by boat to Hejia Granary at the Eastern Capital, then hired carts carried it overland three hundred li to Shan, at a rate of ten cash for every two hu.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Jiang-Huai grain was shipped by boat to Hejia Granary at Luoyang, then hired carts carried it three hundred li overland to Shan, at a cost of ten cash per two hu.

sentences.zh: 耀卿令江、淮舟運悉輸河陰倉，更用河舟運至含嘉倉及太原倉，自太原倉入渭輸關中，凡三歳，運米七百萬斛，省僦車錢三十萬緡。

translations.literal: Yaoji ordered that all Jiang-Huai shipping be delivered to Heyin Granary, then river boats carried it to Hejia and Taiyuan granaries; from Taiyuan Granary it entered the Wei and was transported into Guanzhong. In three years seven million hu of rice were moved, saving three hundred thousand strings in cart hire.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoji required all Jiang-Huai shipping to unload at Heyin Granary, then river boats carried the grain to Hejia and Taiyuan granaries; from Taiyuan it entered the Wei and reached Guanzhong. In three years he moved seven million hu of rice and saved three hundred thousand strings in cart hire.

sentences.zh: 或説耀卿獻所省錢，耀卿曰：「此公家贏縮之利耳，奈何以之市寵乎！

translations.literal: Someone urged Yaoji to present the money saved; Yaoji said: "This is merely the state's surplus or deficit—how could I use it to buy favor!
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Yaoji to present the savings to the throne; he replied: "That is simply the state's operating surplus—how could I trade it for personal favor!

sentences.zh: 」悉奏以爲市糴錢。

translations.literal: " He memorialized that the entire sum be used as funds to purchase grain.
translations.idiomatic: " He reported the full amount for use as grain-purchase funds.

sentences.zh: 張果固請歸恆山，-{制}-以爲銀靑光祿大夫，號通玄先生，厚賜而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhang Guo firmly requested to return to Mount Heng; by imperial order he was made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master of the Palace and styled Master Tongxuan, richly rewarded and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guo insisted on returning to Mount Heng; the Emperor made him Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, styled him Master Tongxuan, gave him lavish gifts, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: -{後}-卒，好異者奏以爲屍解；

translations.literal: Later he died; those fond of the strange memorialized that he had undergone corpse liberation;
translations.idiomatic: He died later, and enthusiasts of the occult reported that he had achieved corpse liberation;

sentences.zh: 上由是頗信神仙。

translations.literal: the Emperor thereby came to believe rather strongly in immortals.
translations.idiomatic: and the Emperor came to believe rather strongly in immortals.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，戊子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on the new moon of wuzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on the wuzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，幽州節度使張守珪斬契丹王屈烈及可突-{干}-，傳首。

translations.literal: On yisi, Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of Youzhou, beheaded the Khitan king Qu Lie and Ketuhan and sent their heads.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Youzhou commissioner Zhang Shougui beheaded the Khitan king Qu Lie and Ketuhan and sent their heads to court.

sentences.zh: 時可突-{干}-連年爲邊患，趙含章、薛楚玉皆不能討。

translations.literal: At that time Ketuhan had for years been a frontier menace; Zhao Hanzhang and Xue Chuyu had both been unable to subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuhan had plagued the frontier for years, and neither Zhao Hanzhang nor Xue Chuyu had been able to defeat him.

sentences.zh: 守珪到官，屢撃破之。

translations.literal: When Shougui took office he repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Shougui took office he defeated Ketuhan again and again.

sentences.zh: 可突-{干}-困迫，遣使詐降，守珪使管記王悔就撫之。

translations.literal: Ketuhan, hard pressed, sent envoys feigning surrender; Shougui sent his registrar Wang Hui to go and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Ketuhan sent envoys feigning surrender; Shougui sent his registrar Wang Hui to accept the submission.

sentences.zh: 悔至其牙帳，察契丹上下初無降意，但稍徙營帳近西北，密遣人引突厥，謀殺悔以叛；

translations.literal: When Hui reached the Khitan royal camp he observed that high and low among the Khitan at first had no intent to submit, but only gradually shifted their camps toward the northwest, secretly sending men to bring in the Turks and plotting to kill Hui and rebel;
translations.idiomatic: At the Khitan royal camp Hui saw that they had no real intent to submit, but were merely shifting camps toward the northwest while secretly summoning the Turks and plotting to kill him and rebel;

sentences.zh: 悔知之。

translations.literal: Hui learned of this.
translations.idiomatic: Hui learned of the plot.

sentences.zh: 牙官李過折與可突-{干}-分典兵馬，爭權不-{葉}-，悔説過折使圖之。

translations.literal: The yabgu officer Li Guozhe and Ketuhan each commanded troops and horses and contended for power without harmony; Hui persuaded Guozhe to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: The yabgu officer Li Guozhe and Ketuhan each commanded troops and were locked in a power struggle; Hui persuaded Guozhe to move against Ketuhan.

sentences.zh: 過折夜勒兵斬屈烈及可突-{干}-，盡誅其黨，帥-{餘}-衆來降。

translations.literal: Guozhe by night led troops and beheaded Qu Lie and Ketuhan, executed their entire faction to the last, and led the remaining multitude to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhe led his troops by night, beheaded Qu Lie and Ketuhan, wiped out their faction, and brought the survivors to surrender.

sentences.zh: 守珪出師紫蒙州，大閲以鎭撫之，梟屈烈、可突-{干}-首-{於}-天津之南。

translations.literal: Shougui marched out from Zimeng Prefecture, held a grand review to pacify them, and displayed the heads of Qu Lie and Ketuhan south of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui marched from Zimeng Prefecture, held a grand review to reassure the tribes, and displayed the heads of Qu Lie and Ketuhan south of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 突厥毘伽可汗爲其大臣梅録啜所毒，未死，討誅梅録啜及其族黨。

translations.literal: The Turkic Bilge Qaghan was poisoned by his minister Meiluo Chuo; before he died he punished and executed Meiluo Chuo and his clan faction.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Bilge Qaghan was poisoned by his minister Meiluo Chuo; before he died he executed Meiluo Chuo and his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 既卒，子伊然可汗立。

translations.literal: After he died, his son Yiran Qaghan was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son Yiran Qaghan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，弟登利可汗立。

translations.literal: Soon he too died, and his younger brother Dengli Qaghan was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died as well, and his younger brother Dengli Qaghan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，來告喪。

translations.literal: On gengxu they came to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu envoys arrived to announce the deaths.

sentences.zh: 禁京城丐者，置病坊以廩之。

translations.literal: Beggars in the capital were forbidden; sick wards were established to supply them with grain.
translations.idiomatic: Begging in the capital was banned, and sick wards were established to feed the destitute.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，契丹知兵馬中郎李過折來獻捷；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Li Guozhe, Khitan director of military affairs, came to present news of victory;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Khitan director of military affairs Li Guozhe came to court with news of victory;

sentences.zh: -{制}-以過折爲北平王，檢校-{松}-漠州都督。

translations.literal: by imperial order Guozhe was made Prince of Beiping and acting military governor of Songmo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and by imperial order he was made Prince of Beiping and acting military governor of Songmo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上耕藉田，九推乃止；

translations.literal: On yihai the Emperor plowed the sacred field, stopping after nine pushes of the plow;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Emperor plowed the sacred field and stopped after nine turns of the plow;

sentences.zh: 公卿以下皆終畝。

translations.literal: the dukes and ministers and those below all finished the acre.
translations.idiomatic: the dukes, ministers, and officials below them each finished an acre.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，都城酺三日。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed for the empire, and the capital held three days of communal feasting.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the capital feasted for three days.

sentences.zh: 上-{御}-五鳳樓酺宴，觀者喧隘，樂不得奏，金吾白梃如雨，不能遏；

translations.literal: The Emperor attended a feast at the Five Phoenixes Tower; the spectators were noisy and crowded, music could not be performed, and the Golden Guard's white clubs fell like rain without being able to restrain them;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held the feast at the Five Phoenixes Tower, but the crowd was so dense and unruly that the music could not be played; the Golden Guard beat the mob with white clubs until they rained down, yet still could not restore order;

sentences.zh: 上患之。

translations.literal: the Emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: and the Emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 髙力士奏河南丞嚴安之爲理嚴，爲人所畏，請使止之；

translations.literal: Gao Lishi memorialized that Henan Assistant Magistrate Yan Anzhi was severe in judgment and feared by men, and requested that he be sent to stop it;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi reported that Henan Assistant Magistrate Yan Anzhi was famously stern and feared, and asked that he be sent to restore order;

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: the Emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 安之至，以手板繞塲畫地曰：「犯此者死！

translations.literal: When Anzhi arrived he used his command tablet to draw a line around the grounds, saying: "Whoever crosses this dies!
translations.idiomatic: When Anzhi arrived he drew a line around the grounds with his command tablet and declared: "Whoever crosses this line dies!

sentences.zh: 」-{於}-是盡三日，人指其畫以相戒，無敢犯者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon for the full three days people pointed to his line to warn one another, and none dared violate it.
translations.idiomatic: " For the full three days people pointed to his line to warn one another, and no one dared cross it.

sentences.zh: 時命三百-{里}-内刺史、縣令各帥所部音樂集-{於}-樓下，各較勝負。

translations.literal: At that time prefects and magistrates within three hundred li were ordered each to lead the musicians of his jurisdiction to assemble below the tower and compete for superiority.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates within three hundred li had each been ordered to bring their local musicians to the tower and compete.

sentences.zh: 懷州刺史上車載樂工數百，皆衣文繡，服箱之牛皆爲虎豹犀象之狀。

translations.literal: The prefect of Huaizhou came in a carriage loaded with several hundred musicians, all dressed in patterned brocade, and the oxen pulling the instrument cases were all shaped like tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Huaizhou arrived in a carriage with several hundred musicians, all in brocade, while the oxen pulling the instrument cases were caparisoned as tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants.

sentences.zh: 魯山令元德秀惟遣樂工數人，連袂歌《-{於}-□》。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Lushan, Yuan Dexiu, sent only a few musicians who, linked arm in arm, sang "Yuwei."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Lushan, Yuan Dexiu, sent only a few musicians who stood arm in arm and sang "Yuwei."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「懷州之人，其塗炭乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Are the people of Huaizhou in charcoal and ashes!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Are the people of Huaizhou being ground to ashes!

sentences.zh: 」立以刺史爲散官。

translations.literal: " He immediately demoted the prefect to an honorary post.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately demoted the prefect to an honorary post.

sentences.zh: 德秀性介潔質-{樸}-，士大夫皆服其髙。

translations.literal: Dexiu's nature was upright, scrupulously clean, and plain; scholar-officials all admired his loftiness.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu was upright, scrupulous, and plain in character, and the scholar-official class admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 上美張守珪之功，欲以爲相，張九齡諫曰：「宰相者，代天理物，非賞功之官也。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired Zhang Shougui's achievements and wished to make him chancellor; Zhang Jiuling remonstrated, saying: "The chancellor is one who assists Heaven in ordering all things—not an office for rewarding merit.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring Zhang Shougui's victories, the Emperor wished to make him chancellor; Zhang Jiuling objected: "The chancellor assists Heaven in ordering the realm—it is not a reward for battlefield merit.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「假以其名而不使任其職，可乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Might one lend him the title without letting him bear the duties—would that do?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked: "Could we give him the title without the duties—would that do?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " He replied: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiuling answered: "No.

sentences.zh: 惟名與器不可以假人，君之所司也。

translations.literal: Titles and regalia must not be lent to others—this is what the ruler oversees.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and regalia must never be lent out—that is the ruler's charge alone.

sentences.zh: 且守珪-{才}-破契丹，陛下即以爲宰相；

translations.literal: Moreover, Shougui has only just defeated the Khitan, and Your Majesty would at once make him chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Shougui has only just defeated the Khitan, and Your Majesty would already make him chancellor;

sentences.zh: 若盡滅奚、厥，將以何官賞之？

translations.literal: if he completely destroys the Xi and Jue, with what office will you reward him?
translations.idiomatic: if he next destroys the Xi and Jue tribes, what office will be left to reward him?

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 二月，守珪詣東都獻捷，拜右羽林大將軍，兼-{御}-史大夫，賜二子官，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: In the second month Shougui went to the Eastern Capital to present his victory, was appointed General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, granted offices to two sons, and richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Shougui came to Luoyang to present his victory, was made General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, had offices granted to two sons, and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 初，殿中侍-{御}-史楊汪既殺張審素，更名萬頃。

translations.literal: Earlier, Palace Disciplinarian Yang Wang, having killed Zhang Shensi, changed his name to Wanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Palace Disciplinarian Yang Wang had killed Zhang Shensi and changed his name to Wanqing.

sentences.zh: 審素二子□、琇皆幼，坐流嶺表；

translations.literal: Shensi's two sons [name missing] and Xiu were both young and were punished by exile to Lingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Shensi's two young sons, [name missing] and Xiu, were exiled to Lingnan;

sentences.zh: 尋逃歸，謀伺便-{復}-仇。

translations.literal: soon they fled back and plotted to watch for an opportunity to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: they soon escaped and plotted to seize a chance for revenge.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁卯，手殺萬頃-{於}-都城。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingmao, they personally killed Wanqing in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingmao, they killed Wanqing with their own hands in the capital.

sentences.zh: -{系}-表-{於}-斧，言父冤狀，欲之江外殺與萬頃同謀陷其父者。

translations.literal: They tied a petition to an axe stating their father's grievance and intended to go beyond the river to kill those who had conspired with Wanqing to frame their father.
translations.idiomatic: They tied a petition to an axe describing their father's wrongful death and set out to kill, beyond the river, those who had conspired with Wanqing to frame him.

sentences.zh: 至汜水，爲有司所得。

translations.literal: When they reached Sishui they were seized by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui they were seized by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 議者多言二子父死非罪，稚年孝烈，能-{復}-父仇，宜加矜宥；

translations.literal: Many who deliberated said the two sons' father had died without guilt, that in their tender years they were filial and fierce and had been able to avenge their father, and that they ought to receive compassionate pardon;
translations.idiomatic: Many argued that their father had died innocent, that the boys, young and fiercely filial, had avenged him, and deserved mercy;

sentences.zh: 張九齡亦欲活之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling also wished to spare their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling too wished to spare them.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿、李林甫以爲如此壞國法，上亦以爲然，謂九齡曰：「孝子之情，義不顧死；

translations.literal: Pei Yaoji and Li Linfu held that this would ruin the laws of the state; the Emperor also thought so, and said to Jiuling: "A filial son's feeling is such that righteousness does not regard death;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaoji and Li Linfu held that this would destroy the law; the Emperor agreed and told Jiuling: "A filial son's passion knows no regard for death;

sentences.zh: 然殺人而赦之，此塗不可啓也。

translations.literal: yet to kill a man and then pardon him—this path must not be opened.
translations.idiomatic: but to kill a man and then pardon the killer— that path must never be opened.

sentences.zh: 」乃下敕曰：「國家設法，期-{於}-止殺。

translations.literal: " He thereupon issued an edict saying: "The state establishes laws in order to stop killing.
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued an edict: "The state establishes laws to end killing.

sentences.zh: 各伸爲子之-{志}-，誰非徇孝之人？

translations.literal: Each would fulfill a son's aim—who is not a man devoted to filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: Every man would act as a son—who is not moved by filial duty?

sentences.zh: 展轉相仇，何有限極！

translations.literal: Revenge passing back and forth—what limit could there be!
translations.idiomatic: Yet if revenge passes back and forth forever, where will it end?

sentences.zh: 咎繇作士，法在必行。

translations.literal: Gao Yao made the Minister of Crime; the law, once made, must be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yao made the Minister of Crime, he meant that law, once proclaimed, must be enforced.

sentences.zh: 曾參殺人，亦不可恕。

translations.literal: Even if Zeng Shen were the killer, he could not be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the killer were Zeng Shen himself, he could not be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 宜付河南府杖殺。

translations.literal: They should be handed over to Henan Prefecture to be beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: They are to be handed over to Henan Prefecture to be beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 」士民皆憐之，爲作哀誄，榜-{於}-衢路。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners all pitied them, composed dirges of mourning, and posted them along the public roads.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and townspeople alike pitied them, wrote elegies in their memory, and posted them at the crossroads.

sentences.zh: 市人斂錢葬之-{於}-北邙。

translations.literal: Market townspeople collected money and buried them on Mount Beimang.
translations.idiomatic: Shopkeepers and townsfolk pooled money to bury them on Mount Beimang north of the capital.

sentences.zh: 恐萬頃家-{發}-之，仍爲作疑塚凡數處。

translations.literal: Fearing the Wanqing family would dig them up, they still made several decoy tombs in various places.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Wanqing family would exhume the bodies, they also raised several false graves in different spots.

sentences.zh: 唐初，公主實封止三百戸，中宗時，太平公主至五千戸，率以七丁爲限。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, a princess's actual fief was limited to three hundred households; in Emperor Zhongzong's time, Princess Taiping reached five thousand households, generally with a limit of seven adult males per household.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang, a princess's substantive fief was capped at three hundred households; under Emperor Zhongzong, Princess Taiping held as many as five thousand, with a general levy of seven adult males per household.

sentences.zh: 開元以來，皇妹止千戸，皇女又半之，皆以三丁爲限；

translations.literal: Since the Kaiyuan era, an emperor's younger sister was limited to one thousand households, an emperor's daughter to half that, all with a limit of three adult males per household;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Kaiyuan reign, an emperor's younger sister received no more than one thousand households and an emperor's daughter half that, each household supplying no more than three adult males;

sentences.zh: 駙馬皆除三品員外官，而不任以職事。

translations.literal: Sons-in-law of the throne were all given nominal third-rank supernumerary posts but were not entrusted with actual duties.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law were all granted nominal third-rank supernumerary titles but given no real responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 公主邑入少，至不能具車服，左右或言其太薄，上曰：「百姓租賦，非我所有。

translations.literal: Princesses' fief income was so small that they could not even fully equip carriages and regalia; attendants sometimes said it was too meager. The Emperor said: "The people's rent and tax are not mine to own.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses' fief income was so slight that some could not even afford full carriages and ceremonial dress, and attendants sometimes complained the allotments were too thin. The Emperor said, "The people's rent and grain are not my private property.

sentences.zh: 戰士出死力，賞不過束帛；

translations.literal: Warriors who risk death receive rewards no greater than bundles of silk;
translations.idiomatic: Fighting men who stake their lives earn rewards no greater than bundles of silk;

sentences.zh: 女子何功，而享多戸邪？

translations.literal: what merit have women, that they should enjoy many households?
translations.idiomatic: what merit have women earned, that they should enjoy so many households?

sentences.zh: 且欲使之知儉嗇耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, I wish to make them know thrift."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I mean them to learn thrift."

sentences.zh: 」秋，七月，-{咸}-宜公主將下嫁，始加實封至千戸。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Princess Xianyi was about to marry; only then was her actual fief increased to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, as Princess Xianyi was about to marry, her substantive fief was for the first time raised to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 公主，武惠妃之女也。

translations.literal: The princess was a daughter of Consort Wu Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was a daughter of Consort Wu Hui.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是諸公主皆加至千戸。

translations.literal: Thereupon all princesses were increased to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every princess received an increase to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊申，突騎施寇北庭及安西拔換城。

translations.literal: Winter, the tenth month, on the day wushen, the Turgesh raided Beiting and Bahuan city in Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day wushen, the Turgesh attacked Beiting and Bahuan city in the Anxi protectorate.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day renyin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the new moon of renyin, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙亥，冊故蜀州司戸楊玄琰女爲壽王妃。

translations.literal: The twelfth month, on the day yihai, the former daughter of Yang Xuanyan, registrar of Shuzhou, was enfeoffed as consort to the Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day yihai, the daughter of the late Yang Xuanyan, registrar of Shuzhou, was invested as consort to the Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: 玄琰，汪之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xuanyan was a great-grandson of Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyan was a great-grandson of Yang Wang.

sentences.zh: 是歳，契丹王過折爲其臣涅禮所殺，-{並}-其諸子，一子刺-{乾}-奔安東得免。

translations.literal: That year, the Khitan king Guozhe was killed by his minister Nieli, who killed all his sons as well; one son, Cigan, fled to Andong and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Khitan king Guozhe was killed by his minister Nieli, who slew all his sons as well; one son, Cigan, fled to Andong and survived.

sentences.zh: 涅禮上言，過折用刑殘虐，衆情不安，故殺之。

translations.literal: Nieli submitted a memorial saying Guozhe's punishments were cruel and brutal, the people's hearts were unsettled, and therefore he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Nieli reported that Guozhe's punishments had been cruel and brutal, the people were uneasy, and for that reason he had killed him.

sentences.zh: 上赦其罪，因以涅禮爲-{松}-漠都督，且賜書責之曰：「卿之蕃法多無義-{於}-君長，自昔如此，朕亦知之。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned his crime and thereupon made Nieli military governor of Songmo, and also sent a letter reproaching him, saying: "Your tribal law often shows no righteousness toward lords and elders; it has been so from old, and I know it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned the crime and appointed Nieli military governor of Songmo, but also sent a letter rebuking him: "Your tribal customs often show little loyalty to lords and elders; that has long been so, and I know it.

sentences.zh: 然過折是卿之王，有惡輒殺之，爲此王者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Yet Guozhe was your king; whenever there was wrong you killed him—how hard it must be to be such a king!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guozhe was your king; whenever you found fault you killed him—how hard must it be to be such a king!

sentences.zh: 但恐卿今爲王，-{後}-人亦爾。

translations.literal: I only fear that now that you are king, those who come after will do the same to you.
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that now you are king, those who follow will treat you the same way.

sentences.zh: 常不自保，誰-{願}-作王！

translations.literal: If one cannot even keep himself safe, who would wish to be king!
translations.idiomatic: If a man cannot even keep himself safe, who would wish to be king!

sentences.zh: 亦應防慮-{後}-事，豈得取快目前！

translations.literal: You should also guard against what comes afterward—how can you seize present satisfaction alone!"
translations.idiomatic: You ought to guard against what comes afterward; how can you satisfy yourself only for the moment!"

sentences.zh: 」突厥尋引兵東侵奚、契丹，涅禮與奚王李歸國共撃破之。

translations.literal: The Turks soon led troops east to invade the Xi and Khitan; Nieli and the Xi king Li Guiguo jointly attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Turks led troops east against the Xi and Khitan; Nieli and the Xi king Li Guiguo joined forces and routed them.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚寅，敕：「天下逃戸，-{聽}-盡今年内自首，有舊産者令還本貫，無者別俟進止；

translations.literal: Spring, the first month, on the day gengyin, an edict: "Fugitive households throughout the realm are permitted to surrender themselves within this year; those with former property are ordered to return to their original registers, those without shall await separate disposition;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day gengyin, an edict declared: "Fugitive households throughout the realm may surrender themselves before the year's end; those who once held property shall return to their original registers, and those without shall await further orders;

sentences.zh: 逾限不首，當命專使搜求，散配諸軍。

translations.literal: those who pass the deadline without surrender shall have special envoys sent to search them out and assign them scattered among the armies.
translations.idiomatic: whoever fails to surrender after the deadline shall be hunted by special commissioners and assigned scattered among the armies.

sentences.zh: 北庭都護蓋嘉運撃突騎施，大破之。

translations.literal: Gai Jiayun, protector-general of Beiting, attacked the Turgesh and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Jiayun, protector-general of Beiting, attacked the Turgesh and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，宴新除縣令-{於}-朝堂，上作《令長新戒》一篇，賜天下縣令。

translations.literal: The second month, on the day jiayin, the Emperor feasted newly appointed county magistrates in the audience hall, composed one piece entitled "New Admonitions for Magistrates," and bestowed it on magistrates throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day jiayin, the Emperor feasted newly appointed county magistrates in the audience hall, composed "New Admonitions for Magistrates," and distributed it to every county magistrate in the realm.

sentences.zh: 庚午，更皇子名：鴻曰瑛，潭曰琮，浚曰璵，洽曰琰，涓曰瑤，滉曰琬，水居曰琚，濰曰璲，沄曰□，澤曰璘，淸曰瑁，回曰玢，沐曰琦，溢曰環，沔曰理，泚曰玼漼曰珪，澄曰珙，潓曰瑱，漎曰璿，滔曰璥。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the imperial sons' names were changed: Hong to Ying, Tan to Cong, Jun to Yu, Xia to Yan, Juan to Yao, Huang to Wan, Shuiju to Ju, Wei to Sui, Yun to [name missing], Ze to Lin, Qing to Mao, Hui to Bin, Mu to Qi, Yi to Huan, Mian to Li, Chi to Ci, Cui to Gui, Cheng to Gong, Hui to Zhen, Long to Xuan, Tao to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu the court renamed the imperial sons: Hong became Ying, Tan became Cong, Jun became Yu, Xia became Yan, Juan became Yao, Huang became Wan, Shuiju became Ju, Wei became Sui, Yun [name missing], Ze became Lin, Qing became Mao, Hui became Bin, Mu became Qi, Yi became Huan, Mian became Li, Chi became Ci, Cui became Gui, Cheng became Gong, Hui became Zhen, Long became Xuan, and Tao became Jin.

sentences.zh: 舊-{制}-，考功員外郎掌試貢舉人。

translations.literal: By old regulation, the assistant director of the Bureau of Appointments supervised the examination of tribute candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, an assistant director in the Bureau of Appointments supervised the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 有進士李權，陵侮員外郎李昂，議者以員外郎位卑，不能服衆；

translations.literal: There was a presented scholar named Li Quan who insulted Assistant Director Li Ang; discussants held that the assistant director's post was too lowly to command the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: When the presented scholar Li Quan insulted Assistant Director Li Ang, critics argued that the post was too low in rank to command respect from the candidates;

sentences.zh: 三月，壬辰，敕自今委禮部侍郎試貢舉人。

translations.literal: the third month, on the day renchen, an edict ordered that from now on the vice minister of rites should conduct the examination of tribute candidates.
translations.idiomatic: in the third month, on the day renchen, an edict ordered that henceforth the vice minister of rites would conduct the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 張守珪使平盧討撃使、左驍衞將軍安祿山討奚、契丹叛者，祿山恃勇輕進，爲虜所敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui sent the Pinglu campaign commissioner and Left Brave Guards general An Lushan to attack Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, relying on his courage, advanced rashly and was defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui sent the Pinglu campaign commissioner and Left Brave Guards general An Lushan against Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, trusting his own bravery, pressed ahead recklessly and was beaten by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，守珪奏請斬之。

translations.literal: Summer, the fourth month, on the day xinhai, Shougui memorialized requesting that he be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinhai, Shougui memorialized asking that Lushan be executed.

sentences.zh: 祿山臨刑呼曰：「大夫不欲滅奚、契丹邪！

translations.literal: As Lushan faced execution he cried out: "My lord, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!
translations.idiomatic: As the execution neared, Lushan cried out, "My lord, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!

sentences.zh: 奈何殺祿山！

translations.literal: Why then kill Lushan!
translations.idiomatic: Why then kill Lushan!

sentences.zh: 」守珪亦惜其驍勇，欲活之，乃更執送京師。

translations.literal: " Shougui also prized his fierce valor and wished to spare him, so he had him bound again and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui too valued his fighting spirit and wished to spare him, so he had him bound once more and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 張九齡批曰：「昔穰苴誅莊賈，孫武斬宮嬪。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling annotated: "In old times Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia, and Sun Wu beheaded palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling wrote in his endorsement: "Long ago Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia, and Sun Wu beheaded the palace women.

sentences.zh: 守珪軍令若行，祿山不宜免死。

translations.literal: If Shougui's military law were enforced, Lushan ought not to escape death."
translations.idiomatic: If Shougui's military law were enforced, Lushan ought not to escape death."

sentences.zh: 」上惜其-{才}-，敕令免官，以白衣將領。

translations.literal: " The Emperor prized his talent, ordered him stripped of office, and employed him as a general in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor prized his ability, ordered him stripped of office, and kept him on as a general in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 九齡固爭曰：「祿山失律喪師，-{於}-法不可不誅。

translations.literal: Jiuling firmly argued: "Lushan violated military law and lost his army; by law he cannot go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling pressed his case: "Lushan broke military law and lost his force; by law he cannot go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 且臣觀其貌有反相，不殺必爲-{後}-患。

translations.literal: Moreover, I observe in his countenance the look of a rebel; if he is not killed he will surely become a trouble afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I see in his face the look of a rebel; if he is not killed he will surely become a scourge later."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿勿以王夷甫識石勒，枉害忠良。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu recognizing Shi Le, wrongly harm a loyal man.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Do not, like Wang Yifu when he recognized Shi Le, wrongly destroy a loyal man.

sentences.zh: 」竟赦之。

translations.literal: " In the end he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 安祿山者，本營州雜胡，初名阿犖山。

translations.literal: An Lushan was originally a mixed barbarian of Yingzhou and was first named Aluoshan.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan was originally a mixed foreigner of Yingzhou and had first been named Aluoshan.

sentences.zh: 其母，巫也；

translations.literal: His mother was a shaman;
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a shaman;

sentences.zh: 父死，母攜之再-{適}-突厥安延偃。

translations.literal: after his father died, his mother took him and remarried the Turk An Yanyan.
translations.idiomatic: after his father died his mother took him and remarried the Turk An Yanyan.

sentences.zh: 會其部落破散，與延偃兄子思順倶逃來，故冒姓安氏，名祿山。

translations.literal: When their tribe was broken and scattered, he fled here together with Yanyan's nephew An Sishun, and therefore took the surname An and the name Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: When their tribe was shattered, he fled with Yanyan's nephew An Sishun and therefore took the surname An and the name Lushan.

sentences.zh: 又有史窣-{干}-者，與祿山同裡閉，先-{後}-一日生。

translations.literal: There was also one named Shi Suogan, born in the same neighborhood as Lushan, one day before or after him.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a man named Shi Suogan, born in the same neighborhood as Lushan a day apart.

sentences.zh: 及長，相親愛，皆爲互市牙郎，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: When grown, they were close and affectionate; both became brokers in the border markets and were known for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: When they grew up they were close friends; both became brokers in the border markets and were known for their fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 張守珪以祿山爲捉生將，祿山毎與數騎出，輒擒契丹數十人而返。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui made Lushan a captive-taking officer; each time Lushan went out with several horsemen he would seize several dozen Khitan and return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui made Lushan a captive-taking officer; whenever Lushan rode out with a few horsemen he would seize dozens of Khitan and return.

sentences.zh: 狡黠，善揣人情，守珪愛之，養以爲子。

translations.literal: Cunning and sly, skilled at reading men's hearts, Shougui loved him and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning and skilled at reading men, Shougui favored him and raised him as a son.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-嘗負官債亡入奚中，爲奚-{游}-弈所得，欲殺之；

translations.literal: Suogan once owed an official debt and fled into Xi territory; he was seized by a Xi patrol and they wished to kill him;
translations.idiomatic: Suogan once fled into Xi territory to escape an official debt; a Xi patrol seized him and meant to kill him;

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-紿曰：「我，唐之和親使也。

translations.literal: Suogan deceived them, saying: "I am Tang's marriage-peace envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Suogan deceived them, saying, "I am Tang's marriage envoy.

sentences.zh: 汝殺我，禍且及汝國。

translations.literal: If you kill me, disaster will reach your state as well.
translations.idiomatic: If you kill me, disaster will reach your state as well.

sentences.zh: 」-{游}-弈信之，送詣牙帳。

translations.literal: " The patrol believed him and sent him to the royal tent.
translations.idiomatic: The patrol believed him and sent him to the royal tent.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-見奚王，長揖不拜，奚王雖怒，而畏唐，不敢殺，以客禮館之，使百人隨窣-{干}-入朝。

translations.literal: Suogan saw the Xi king, made a long bow but did not prostrate himself; though the Xi king was angry, he feared Tang and did not dare kill him, lodged him with guest rites, and sent a hundred men to follow Suogan to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Suogan met the Xi king he bowed from the waist but would not kowtow; though the king was angry, he feared Tang and did not dare kill him, housed him as a guest, and sent a hundred men to follow Suogan to court.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-謂奚王曰：「王所遣人雖多，觀其-{才}-皆不足以見天子。

translations.literal: Suogan said to the Xi king: "Though the men you send are many, judging their talent none is fit to see the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Suogan told the Xi king, "Though you send many men, none of them has talent enough to see the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 聞王有良將瑣髙者，何不使之入朝！

translations.literal: I hear you have a fine general named Suogao—why not send him to court!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have a fine general named Suogao—why not send him to court!"

sentences.zh: 」奚王即命瑣髙與牙下三百人隨窣-{干}-入朝。

translations.literal: " The Xi king at once ordered Suogao and three hundred men under his command to follow Suogan to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi king at once ordered Suogao and three hundred warriors under his command to follow Suogan to court.

sentences.zh: 窣-{干}-將至平盧，先使人謂軍使裴休子曰：「奚使瑣髙與精鋭倶來，聲-{雲}-入朝，實欲襲軍城，宜謹爲之備，先事圖之。

translations.literal: Before Suogan reached Pinglu he first sent a man to tell the army commissioner Pei Xiuzi: "The Xi envoy Suogao is coming with picked troops; though they claim to be entering court, they truly intend to strike the garrison city—you should prepare carefully and act first."
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching Pinglu, Suogan sent word to the army commissioner Pei Xiuzi: "The Xi envoy Suogao is coming with picked troops; though they claim to be entering court, they truly mean to strike the garrison—you must prepare carefully and strike first."

sentences.zh: 」休子乃具軍容出迎，至館，悉坑殺其從兵，執瑣髙送幽州。

translations.literal: " Xiuzi thereupon arrayed his troops in full order to go out and receive them; when they reached the lodge he buried alive all their followers, seized Suogao, and sent him to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzi arrayed his troops and went out to receive them; at the lodge he slaughtered all the followers and sent Suogao captive to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 張守珪以窣-{干}-爲有功，奏爲果毅，累遷將軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Shougui, holding that Suogan had rendered merit, memorialized to make him a guoyi officer, and he was repeatedly promoted to general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui, crediting Suogan with merit, memorialized to appoint him a guoyi officer, and he rose through the ranks to general.

sentences.zh: -{後}-入奏事，上與語，悅之，賜名思明。

translations.literal: Later, when he entered to report affairs, the Emperor spoke with him, was pleased, and bestowed the name Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he came to report at court, the Emperor spoke with him, was pleased, and bestowed the name Siming.

sentences.zh: 故連州司馬武攸望之子温愼，坐交通權貴，杖死。

translations.literal: Wen Shen, son of the former Lianzhou aide Wu Youwang, was punished for associating with powerful nobles and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shen, son of the former Lianzhou aide Wu Youwang, was punished for trafficking with powerful nobles and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 乙-{丑}-，朔方、河東節度使信安王禕貶衢州刺史，廣武王承宏貶房州別駕，涇州刺史薛自勸貶澧州別駕；

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Xin'an Prince Li Yi, military governor of Shuofang and Hedong, was demoted to prefect of Quzhou; Prince of Guangwu Li Chenghong was demoted to assistant prefect of Fangzhou; Xue Ziqin, prefect of Jingzhou, was demoted to assistant prefect of Lizhou;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, Xin'an Prince Li Yi, military governor of Shuofang and Hedong, was demoted to prefect of Quzhou; Prince of Guangwu Li Chenghong was demoted to assistant prefect of Fangzhou; and Xue Ziqin, prefect of Jingzhou, was demoted to assistant prefect of Lizhou;

sentences.zh: 皆坐與温愼交-{遊}-故也。

translations.literal: all because they had associated and traveled with Wen Shen.
translations.idiomatic: all for having associated with Wen Shen.

sentences.zh: 承宏，守禮之子也。

translations.literal: Chenghong was a son of Li Shouli.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghong was a son of Li Shouli.

sentences.zh: 辛未，蒲州刺史王琚貶通州刺史；

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Wang Ju, prefect of Pu, was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, Wang Ju, prefect of Pu, was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou;

sentences.zh: 坐禕交書也。

translations.literal: because he had exchanged letters with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: for having exchanged letters with Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 五月，醴泉妖人劉-{志}-誠作亂，驅掠路人，將趣-{咸}-陽。

translations.literal: The fifth month, the sorcerer Liu Zhicheng of Liquan raised a disturbance, driving and plundering passersby, intending to press toward Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the sorcerer Liu Zhicheng of Liquan raised a disturbance, driving and plundering travelers as he marched toward Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 邨民走告縣官，焚橋斷路以拒之，其衆遂潰。

translations.literal: Villagers ran to inform the county officials, burned bridges and cut roads to resist them, and his band thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers ran to warn the county magistrate, burned bridges and blocked the roads to stop them, and the band soon scattered.

sentences.zh: 數日，悉擒斬之。

translations.literal: Within several days all were seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Within days all were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 六月，初分月給百官俸錢。

translations.literal: The sixth month, for the first time officials' salary cash was distributed by the month.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the court for the first time paid officials' salaries in monthly installments.

sentences.zh: 初，上因藉田赦，命有司議增宗廟籩豆之-{薦}-及服紀未通者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor granted an amnesty at the plowing ceremony, he ordered the relevant offices to discuss increasing the offerings of baskets and stands in the ancestral temple and matters of mourning garb not yet harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in an amnesty proclaimed at the plowing ceremony, the Emperor had ordered the relevant offices to discuss increasing the offerings placed before the ancestral temple and unresolved matters of mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 太常卿韋縚奏請宗廟毎坐籩豆十二。

translations.literal: Wei Tao, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized requesting twelve baskets and stands at each seat in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tao, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized asking that twelve baskets and stands be set before each seat in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎張均、職方郎中韋述議曰：「聖人知孝人之情深而物類之無限，故爲之節-{制}-。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun and Director of Posts Wei Shu argued: "The sage knew that a filial son's feeling runs deep while the kinds of things are limitless, and therefore set regulations for it.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun and Director of Posts Wei Shu argued: "The sages knew that a filial son's devotion runs deep while the kinds of offerings are limitless, and therefore set regulations.

sentences.zh: 人之嗜好本無憑準，宴私之饌與時遷移，故聖人一切同歸-{於}-古。

translations.literal: Men's appetites in themselves have no fixed standard; private feast foods shift with the times, and therefore the sages made everything alike return to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Human taste has no fixed standard; foods for private feasts change with the age, and therefore the sages made all offerings conform to ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 屈到嗜芰，屈建不以-{薦}-，以爲不以私慾-{干}-國之典。

translations.literal: Qu Dao loved water chestnuts, but Qu Jian did not offer them in sacrifice, holding that private desire must not disturb the state's canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Dao loved water chestnuts, but Qu Jian would not offer them in sacrifice, holding that private appetite must not disturb the state's canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 今欲取甘旨肥濃，皆充祭用，苟逾舊-{制}-，其何限焉！

translations.literal: Now if you wish to take every sweet delicacy and rich savory and make them all offerings, once you exceed the old regulation, where would the limit be!
translations.idiomatic: If every sweet delicacy and rich savory is to be pressed into sacrificial use, and the old regulation is exceeded, where would the limit lie!

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'It is not the millet and sacrificial grain that are fragrant; bright virtue alone is fragrant.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "It is not millet and sacrificial grain that are fragrant; bright virtue alone is fragrant."

sentences.zh: 』若以今之珍饌，平生所習，求神無方，何必泥古，則簠簋可去而盤盂杯案當在-{御}-矣，韶濩可息而箜篌箏笛當在奏矣。

translations.literal: ' If, taking today's rare foods and what one is used to in life, you say that in seeking the spirits there is no fixed method and there is no need to cling to antiquity, then the grain vessels could be removed and platters, cups, and trays should be set out instead; the Shao and Hu music could cease and the konghou, zheng, and flute should be played.
translations.idiomatic: If today's delicacies and one's lifelong habits are enough, and in seeking the spirits there is no fixed method and no need to cling to antiquity, then the grain vessels could be discarded and platters, cups, and trays set out instead; the Shao and Hu could fall silent while konghou, zheng, and flutes took their place.

sentences.zh: 既非正物，-{後}-嗣何觀！

translations.literal: Since these are not the proper things, what would later generations behold!
translations.idiomatic: Since these are not the proper things, what would later generations behold!

sentences.zh: 夫神，以精明臨人者也，不求-{豐}-大；

translations.literal: The spirits, by their keen insight, oversee men; they do not seek abundance and grandeur;
translations.idiomatic: The spirits oversee men through keen insight; they do not seek abundance and grandeur;

sentences.zh: 苟失-{於}-禮，雖多何爲！

translations.literal: if the rites are lost, of what use is abundance!
translations.idiomatic: if the rites are lost, what good is abundance!

sentences.zh: 豈可廢棄禮經以從流俗！

translations.literal: How can one abandon the ritual classics to follow passing fashion!
translations.idiomatic: How can one abandon the ritual classics to follow passing fashion!

sentences.zh: 且君子愛人以禮，不求苟合；

translations.literal: Moreover, the gentleman loves others through ritual and does not seek careless compliance;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the gentleman loves others through ritual and does not seek careless compliance;

sentences.zh: 況在宗廟，敢忘舊章？

translations.literal: how much more in the ancestral temple—who would dare forget the old statutes?"
translations.idiomatic: how much less in the ancestral temple—who would dare forget the old statutes?"

sentences.zh: 太子賓客崔沔議曰：「祭祀之興，肇-{於}-太古。

translations.literal: Cui Hao, guest of the heir apparent, argued: "The rise of sacrifice began in utmost antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, guest of the heir apparent, argued: "Sacrifice arose in utmost antiquity.

sentences.zh: 茹毛飲血，則有毛血之-{薦}-；

translations.literal: When men ate raw flesh and drank blood, there were offerings of fur and blood;
translations.idiomatic: When men ate raw flesh and drank blood, there were offerings of fur and blood;

sentences.zh: 未有-{麴}-薛，則有玄酒之奠。

translations.literal: before there was leavened grain and yeast, there was the offering of dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: before there was leavened grain and yeast, there was the offering of dark wine.

sentences.zh: 施及-{後}-王，禮物漸備；

translations.literal: Extending to later kings, ritual objects gradually became complete;
translations.idiomatic: Under later kings ritual objects gradually became complete;

sentences.zh: 然以神道致敬，不敢廢也。

translations.literal: yet in reverence through the way of the spirits they did not dare abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: yet in reverence to the spirits they did not dare abolish the older offerings.

sentences.zh: 籩豆簠簋樽罍之實，皆周人之時饌也，其用通-{於}-宴饗賓客，而周公-{制}-禮，與毛血玄酒同-{薦}-鬼神。

translations.literal: The contents of baskets, stands, grain vessels, and wine jars were all foods of Zhou times; their use extended to feasts and entertaining guests, yet the Duke of Zhou made ritual and offered them to the spirits together with fur, blood, and dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: The contents of baskets, stands, grain vessels, and wine jars were foods of Zhou times, used alike at feasts and for entertaining guests, yet the Duke of Zhou established ritual and offered them to the spirits together with fur, blood, and dark wine.

sentences.zh: 國家由禮立訓，因時-{制}--{范}-，淸廟時饗，禮饌必陳，用周-{制}-也。

translations.literal: The state establishes instruction through ritual and shapes regulations and standards to the times; at seasonal offerings in the Pure Temple, ritual foods must be set out—this follows Zhou regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The state establishes instruction through ritual and shapes regulations and standards to the times; at seasonal offerings in the Pure Temple, ritual foods must be set out—this follows Zhou practice.

sentences.zh: 園寢上食，時膳具設，遵漢法也。

translations.literal: At park-tombs the presentation of food, with seasonal viands all set out, follows Han law.
translations.idiomatic: At the park-tombs the presentation of food, with seasonal viands fully set out, follows Han practice.

sentences.zh: 職貢來祭，致遠物也。

translations.literal: When tribute offices come to sacrifice, they present things brought from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute offices come to sacrifice, they present goods brought from afar.

sentences.zh: 有新必-{薦}-，順時令也。

translations.literal: Whenever there is something new it must be offered—that is following the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there is something new it must be offered—that is observing the seasons.

sentences.zh: 苑囿之内，躬稼所收，搜狩之時，親-{發}-所中，莫不-{薦}-而-{後}-食，盡誠敬也。

translations.literal: Within the parks and preserves, what was reaped from the ruler's own plowing, and at the hunt what the ruler personally shot—none of it was eaten before being offered; that is utmost sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Within the imperial parks, grain from the Emperor's own plowing and game from his own bow at the hunt were all offered before being eaten—such was the fullness of sincerity and reverence.

sentences.zh: 若此至矣，-{復}-何加焉！

translations.literal: If it has reached this point, what more could be added!
translations.idiomatic: When devotion has reached this point, what more could be added!

sentences.zh: 但當申敕有司，無或簡怠，則鮮美肥濃，盡在是矣，不必加籩豆之數也。

translations.literal: One need only charge the responsible offices sternly that none be remiss or negligent; then every fresh delicacy and rich savory will be fully provided—there is no need to increase the number of baskets and stands.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices need only be charged sternly not to be remiss or negligent; then every fresh delicacy and rich savory will be fully provided—there is no need to increase the number of baskets and stands.

sentences.zh: 上固欲量加品味。

translations.literal: The Emperor still wished to add offerings in measured degree.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor still wished to add offerings in some measure.

sentences.zh: 縚又奏毎室加籩豆各六，四時各實以新果珍羞；

translations.literal: Wei Tao again memorialized that six baskets and stands be added before each seat, and that in each of the four seasons they be filled with fresh fruit and rare delicacies;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tao again memorialized that six baskets and stands be added before each seat, filled in each of the four seasons with fresh fruit and rare delicacies;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 縚又奏：「《喪服》『舅，緦麻三月，從母，外祖父母皆小功五月。

translations.literal: Wei Tao again memorialized: "The Mourning Garments states: 'For an uncle, sizang mourning for three months; for a mother's sister and for maternal grandparents, xiaogong mourning for five months.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tao again memorialized: "The Mourning Garments states, "For an uncle, sizang mourning for three months; for a mother's sister and for maternal grandparents, xiaogong mourning for five months.

sentences.zh: 』外祖至尊，同-{於}-從母之服；

translations.literal: ' The maternal grandfather, though supremely honored, wears the same mourning as a mother's sister;
translations.idiomatic: " The maternal grandfather, though supremely honored, wears the same mourning as a mother's sister;

sentences.zh: 姨、舅一等，服則輕重有殊。

translations.literal: aunt and uncle are of one rank, yet their mourning garments differ in weight.
translations.idiomatic: yet aunt and uncle are of one rank while their mourning garments differ in weight.

sentences.zh: 堂姨、舅親即未疎，恩絶不相爲服，舅母來承外族，不如同爨之禮。

translations.literal: Paternal cousins among aunts and uncles are not yet distant in kinship, yet affection is cut off and they do not wear mourning for one another; an uncle's wife, coming to join the outer clan, is treated less favorably than those who shared the same hearth.
translations.idiomatic: Paternal cousins among aunts and uncles are not yet distant in kinship, yet no mourning is worn for one another; an uncle's wife, joining the outer clan, is treated less favorably than those who shared the same hearth.

sentences.zh: 竊以古意猶有所未暢者也，請加外祖父母爲大功九月，姨、舅皆小功五月，堂舅、堂姨、舅母-{並}-加至袒免。

translations.literal: I venture to think that the ancient meaning still has points not fully expressed; I request that maternal grandparents be raised to dagong mourning for nine months, that aunts and uncles all receive xiaogong mourning for five months, and that paternal uncles, paternal aunts, and uncles' wives all be raised to taboo mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think the ancient meaning still has points not fully expressed; I request that maternal grandparents be raised to dagong mourning for nine months, that aunts and uncles all receive xiaogong mourning for five months, and that paternal uncles, paternal aunts, and uncles' wives all be raised to taboo mourning.

sentences.zh: 崔沔議曰：「正家之道，不可以貳；

translations.literal: Cui Mian argued: "The way to set the household in order cannot be twofold;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mian argued: "The way to set the household in order cannot be twofold;

sentences.zh: 總一定義，理歸本宗。

translations.literal: when principle is gathered into one fixed meaning, reason returns to the main lineage.
translations.idiomatic: when principle is gathered into one fixed meaning, reason returns to the main lineage.

sentences.zh: 是以内有齊、斬，外皆緦麻，尊名所加，不過一等，此先王不易之道也。

translations.literal: Therefore within there are qi and zhan mourning, while without all is sizang; where honor adds to a name, it does not exceed one grade—this is the unchanging way of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore within the family there are qi and zhan mourning, while without all is sizang; where honor adds to a name, it does not exceed one grade—this is the unchanging way of the former kings.

sentences.zh: -{願}-守八年明旨，一依古禮，以爲萬代成法。

translations.literal: I wish to uphold the clear decree of the eighth year and follow the ancient rites alone, making them the established law for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to uphold the clear decree of the eighth year and follow the ancient rites alone, making them the established law for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 韋述議曰：「《喪服傳》曰：『禽獸知母而不知父。

translations.literal: Wei Shu argued: "The Commentary on Mourning Garments says: 'Beasts know their mother but not their father.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu argued: "The Commentary on Mourning Garments says, "Beasts know their mother but not their father.

sentences.zh: 野人曰，父母何等焉！

translations.literal: The rustic says, How can father and mother be equal!
translations.idiomatic: The rustic says, How can father and mother be equal!

sentences.zh: 都邑之士則知尊檷矣；

translations.literal: The gentleman of the capital knows how to honor his father;
translations.idiomatic: The townsman of the capital knows how to honor his father;

sentences.zh: 大夫及學士則知尊祖矣。

translations.literal: the grandee and the scholar know how to honor their ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: the grandee and the scholar know how to honor their ancestors.

sentences.zh: 』聖人究天道而厚-{於}-祖檷，-{系}-族姓而親其子孫，母黨比-{於}-本族，不可同貫，明矣。

translations.literal: ' The sage exhausts the way of Heaven and is deep toward ancestors and father; he ties clan surnames and cherishes their descendants—the mother's kin compared with the main clan cannot be treated as one thread; this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: " The sage exhausts the way of Heaven and is deep toward ancestors and father; he ties clan surnames and cherishes their descendants—the mother's kin compared with the main clan cannot be treated as one thread; this is clear.

sentences.zh: 今三子皆已成人，不聞大過，陛下奈何一旦以無根之語，喜怒之際，盡廢之乎！

translations.literal: Now all three sons are grown men, and no great fault is heard of them—how can Your Majesty, in a moment of anger and joy, on groundless words, depose them all!
translations.idiomatic: Now all three sons are grown men, and no great fault is heard of them—how can Your Majesty, in a moment of anger, on groundless words, depose them all!

sentences.zh: 且太子天下本，不可輕搖。

translations.literal: Moreover, the crown prince is the root of all under Heaven and must not be lightly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the crown prince is the root of the realm and must not be lightly shaken.

sentences.zh: 昔晉獻公-{聽}-驪姬之讒殺申生，三世大亂。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin heeded Lady Li's slander and killed Prince Shensheng, and three generations fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin heeded Lady Li's slander and killed Prince Shensheng, and three generations fell into great disorder.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝信江充之誣罪戾太子，京城流血。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's false charge against the heir apparent and blood flowed in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's false charge against the heir apparent, and blood flowed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝用賈-{後}-之譖廢愍懷太子，中原塗炭。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin took Empress Jia's slander and deposed the heir apparent Minhuai, and the central plains were laid waste.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin took Empress Jia's slander and deposed Crown Prince Minhuai, and the central plains were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝納獨孤-{後}-之言黜太子勇，立煬帝，遂失天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui accepted Empress Dugu's words, removed Crown Prince Yong, and enthroned Emperor Yang, and thus lost all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui accepted Empress Dugu's words, removed Crown Prince Yong, and enthroned Emperor Yang, and thus lost the realm.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，不可不愼。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, one cannot but be careful.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this, one cannot but be careful.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲爲此，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty insists on doing this, your servant dares not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on doing this, your servant dares not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 」上不悅。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 林甫初無所言，退而私謂宦官之貴幸者曰：「此主上家事，何必問外人！

translations.literal: Li Linfu at first said nothing; after withdrawing he privately told a favored eunuch: "This is the sovereign's own family affair—why must outsiders be consulted!
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu at first said nothing; after withdrawing he privately told a favored eunuch, "This is the sovereign's own family affair—why must outsiders be consulted!

sentences.zh: 」上猶豫未決。

translations.literal: " The Emperor hesitated and had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor hesitated and had not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 惠妃密使官奴牛貴兒謂九齡曰：「有廢必有興，公爲之援，宰相可長處。

translations.literal: Consort Hui secretly sent the official slave Niu Guier to tell Zhang Jiuling: "Where there is deposition there must be elevation; if you lend your support, you may long hold the post of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Hui secretly sent the official slave Niu Guier to tell Zhang Jiuling, "Where there is deposition there must be elevation; if you lend your support, you may long hold the post of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」九齡叱之，以其語白上；

translations.literal: " Zhang Jiuling rebuked him and reported his words to the Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jiuling rebuked him and reported his words to the Emperor;

sentences.zh: 上爲之動色，故訖九齡罷相，太子得無動。

translations.literal: the Emperor's expression changed at this, and so until Zhang Jiuling was removed as chief minister the crown prince remained unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor's expression changed at this, and so until Zhang Jiuling was removed as chief minister the crown prince remained unmoved.

sentences.zh: 林甫日夜短九齡-{於}-上，上浸疎之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu day and night spoke ill of Zhang Jiuling to the Emperor, and the Emperor gradually grew distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu day and night spoke ill of Zhang Jiuling to the Emperor, and the Emperor gradually grew distant from him.

sentences.zh: 林甫引蕭炅爲戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: Li Linfu brought in Xiao Jiong as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu brought in Xiao Jiong as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 炅素不學，嘗對中書侍郎嚴挺之讀「伏-{臘}-」爲「伏獵」。

translations.literal: Jiong had never studied and once, facing Secretariat Vice Director Yan Tingzhi, read "fu-la" (winter and summer sacrifices) as "fu-lie" (crouching to hunt).
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had never studied and once, facing Secretariat Vice Director Yan Tingzhi, read fu-la (winter and summer sacrifices) as fu-lie (crouching to hunt).

sentences.zh: 挺之言-{於}-九齡曰：「省中豈容有『伏獵侍郎』！

translations.literal: Tingzhi spoke to Zhang Jiuling, saying: "How can the Secretariat tolerate a 'Crouching Hunt Vice Minister'!
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi spoke to Zhang Jiuling, saying, "How can the Secretariat tolerate a 'Crouching Hunt Vice Minister'!

sentences.zh: 」由是出炅爲岐州刺史，故林甫怨挺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jiong was sent out as prefect of Qizhou, and so Li Linfu resented Tingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Jiong was sent out as prefect of Qizhou, and so Li Linfu resented Tingzhi.

sentences.zh: 九齡與挺之善，欲引以爲相，嘗謂之曰：「李尚書方承恩，足下宜一造門，與之款暱。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling was on good terms with Tingzhi and wished to bring him in as chief minister; he once told him: "Minister Li is just now enjoying favor—you should pay one visit to his door and become close with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling was on good terms with Tingzhi and wished to bring him in as chief minister; he once told him, "Minister Li is just now enjoying favor—you should pay one visit to his door and become close with him.

sentences.zh: 」挺之素負氣，薄林甫爲人，竟不之詣；

translations.literal: " Tingzhi had always been proud of spirit and looked down on Li Linfu's character; in the end he did not go;
translations.idiomatic: " Tingzhi had always been proud of spirit and looked down on Li Linfu's character; in the end he did not go;

sentences.zh: 林甫恨之益深。

translations.literal: and Li Linfu hated him all the more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Linfu hated him all the more deeply.

sentences.zh: 挺之先娶妻，出之，更嫁蔚州刺史王元琰，元琰坐贓罪下三司按鞫，挺之爲之營解。

translations.literal: Tingzhi had earlier taken a wife and divorced her; she remarried Wang Yuanyan, prefect of Yu Prefecture. Yuanyan was charged with corruption and sent down to the Three Offices for investigation; Tingzhi worked to secure his release on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi had earlier taken a wife and divorced her; she remarried Wang Yuanyan, prefect of Yu Prefecture. Yuanyan was charged with corruption and sent down to the Three Offices for investigation; Tingzhi worked to secure his release on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 林甫因左右使-{於}-禁中白上。

translations.literal: Li Linfu used those close at hand to report this to the Emperor within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu used those close at hand to report this to the Emperor within the palace.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相曰：「挺之爲罪人請屬所由。

translations.literal: The Emperor told the chief ministers: "Tingzhi is pleading on behalf of a criminal with those who handle the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the chief ministers, "Tingzhi is pleading on behalf of a criminal with those who handle the case.

sentences.zh: 」九齡曰：「此乃挺之出妻，不宜有情。

translations.literal: " Zhang Jiuling said: "This is Tingzhi's divorced wife; he ought not to harbor affection.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jiuling said, "This is Tingzhi's divorced wife; he ought not to harbor affection.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「雖離乃-{復}-有私。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Though divorced, he still has private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Though divorced, he still has private feeling.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是上積前事，以耀卿、九齡爲阿黨；

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor piled up earlier matters and treated Yaoji and Jiuling as a clique;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Emperor piled up earlier matters and treated Yaoji and Jiuling as a clique;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以耀爲左丞相，九齡爲右丞相，-{並}-罷政事。

translations.literal: on renyin he made Yaoji Left Chief Minister and Jiuling Right Chief Minister, and both were removed from active government.
translations.idiomatic: on renyin he made Yaoji Left Chief Minister and Jiuling Right Chief Minister, and both were removed from active government.

sentences.zh: 以林甫兼中書令；

translations.literal: Li Linfu was made concurrent Secretariat Director;
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu was made concurrent Secretariat Director;

sentences.zh: 仙客爲工部尚書、同中書門下三品，鄰朔方節度如故。
