translations.literal: Xianke was made Minister of Works and Associate Secretariat Director of the Third Rank, still retaining his Shuofang command as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke was made Minister of Works and Associate Secretariat Director of the Third Rank, still retaining his Shuofang command as before.

sentences.zh: 嚴挺之貶洺州刺史，王元琰流嶺南。

translations.literal: Yan Tingzhi was demoted to prefect of Ming Prefecture, and Wang Yuanyan was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi was demoted to prefect of Ming Prefecture, and Wang Yuanyan was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 上即位以來，所用之相，姚崇尚通，宋珪尚法，張嘉貞尚吏，張説尚文，李元紘、杜暹尚儉，韓休、張九齡尚直，各其所長也。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor took the throne, the chief ministers he has used each had their strength: Yao Chong valued comprehensiveness, Song Jing valued law, Zhang Jiazhen valued administration, Zhang Yue valued letters, Li Yuanhong and Du Xian valued frugality, Han Xiu and Zhang Jiuling valued uprightness—each his own forte.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Emperor took the throne, the chief ministers he had used each had their strength: Yao Chong valued comprehensiveness, Song Jing valued law, Zhang Jiazhen valued administration, Zhang Yue valued letters, Li Yuanhong and Du Xian valued frugality, Han Xiu and Zhang Jiuling valued uprightness—each his own forte.

sentences.zh: 九齡既得罪，自是朝廷之士，皆容身保位，無-{復}-直言。

translations.literal: Once Zhang Jiuling had fallen from favor, from then on the men of court all sheltered themselves and guarded their posts, and none again spoke plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Jiuling had fallen from favor, from then on the men of court all sheltered themselves and guarded their posts, and none again spoke plainly.

sentences.zh: 李林甫欲蔽塞人主視-{聽}-，自專大權，明召諸諫官謂曰：「今明主在上，群臣將順之不暇，烏用多言！

translations.literal: Li Linfu wished to block the sovereign lord's sight and hearing and monopolize great power; he openly summoned the remonstrance officials and said: "Now a brilliant sovereign is above; the ministers can scarcely keep pace in yielding to him—what use is much talk!
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu wished to block the sovereign lord's sight and hearing and monopolize great power; he openly summoned the remonstrance officials and said, "Now a brilliant sovereign is above; the ministers can scarcely keep pace in yielding to him—what use is much talk!

sentences.zh: 諸君不見立仗馬乎？

translations.literal: Do you gentlemen not see the horses of the palace guard formation?
translations.idiomatic: Do you gentlemen not see the horses of the palace guard formation?

sentences.zh: 食三品料，一鳴輒斥去，悔之何及！

translations.literal: They eat third-rank rations; one neigh and they are driven away—how can regret come in time!
translations.idiomatic: They eat third-rank rations; one neigh and they are driven away—how can regret come in time!

sentences.zh: 補闕杜璡嘗上書言事，明日，黜爲下邽令。

translations.literal: Palace Remonstrator Du Lin once submitted a memorial on state affairs; the next day he was demoted to magistrate of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Remonstrator Du Lin once submitted a memorial on state affairs; the next day he was demoted to magistrate of Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 自是諫爭路絶矣。

translations.literal: From then on the road of remonstrance and dispute was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the road of remonstrance and dispute was cut off.

sentences.zh: 牛仙客既爲林甫所引進，專給唯諾而已。

translations.literal: Niu Xianke, having been brought in by Li Linfu, did nothing but supply yeses and nos.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xianke, having been brought in by Li Linfu, did nothing but supply yeses and nos.

sentences.zh: 然二人皆謹守格式，百官遷除，各有常度，雖奇-{才}-異行，不免終老常調；

translations.literal: Yet the two men both strictly observed regulations and forms; promotions and removals of the hundred officials each had their fixed measure, and even men of rare talent and unusual conduct could not escape ending their days in routine appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two men both strictly observed regulations and forms; promotions and removals of the hundred officials each had their fixed measure, and even men of rare talent and unusual conduct could not escape ending their days in routine appointments;

sentences.zh: 其以巧諂邪險自進者，則超騰不次，自有它蹊矣。

translations.literal: those who advanced by crafty flattery, wickedness, and treachery, however, leaped up out of order and had their own other paths.
translations.idiomatic: those who advanced by crafty flattery, wickedness, and treachery, however, leaped up out of order and had their own other paths.

sentences.zh: 林甫城府深密，人莫窺其際。

translations.literal: Li Linfu's mind was a deep and sealed fortress; no one could glimpse its bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu's mind was a deep and sealed fortress; no one could glimpse its bounds.

sentences.zh: 好以甘言啖人，而陰中傷之，不露辭色。

translations.literal: He liked to feed men with sweet words while secretly striking them down, without revealing it in speech or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to feed men with sweet words while secretly striking them down, without revealing it in speech or countenance.

sentences.zh: 凡爲上所厚者，始則親結之，及位勢稍逼，輒以計去之。

translations.literal: All whom the Emperor favored he would at first draw close and bind to himself; once rank and power drew slightly near, he would remove them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: All whom the Emperor favored he would at first draw close and bind to himself; once rank and power drew slightly near, he would remove them by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 雖老-{奸}-巨猾，無能逃其-{術}-者。

translations.literal: Even old villains and great rogues could not escape his methods.
translations.idiomatic: Even old villains and great rogues could not escape his methods.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，初置玄學博士，毎歳依明經舉。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the post of Doctor of the Learning of the Mysterious was first established; each year candidates were raised by the same method as for the Classicist degree.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the post of Doctor of the Learning of the Mysterious was first established; each year candidates were raised by the same method as for the Classicist degree.

sentences.zh: 二月，敕曰：「進士以聲韻爲學，多昧古今；

translations.literal: In the second month an edict said: "Jinshi scholars take tonal prosody as their study and are mostly ignorant of past and present;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month an edict said, "Jinshi scholars take tonal prosody as their study and are mostly ignorant of past and present;

sentences.zh: 明經以貼誦爲功，罕窮旨趣。

translations.literal: Classicists take pasted recitation as their achievement and rarely penetrate the essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Classicists take pasted recitation as their achievement and rarely penetrate the essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 自今明經問大義十條，對時務策三首；

translations.literal: From now on Classicists shall be questioned on ten items of great principle and answer three policy essays on current affairs;
translations.idiomatic: From now on Classicists shall be questioned on ten items of great principle and answer three policy essays on current affairs;

sentences.zh: 進士試大經十貼。

translations.literal: jinshi candidates shall be tested on ten pasted passages from the great classics.
translations.idiomatic: jinshi candidates shall be tested on ten pasted passages from the great classics.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，新羅王興光卒，子承慶襲位。

translations.literal: On wuchen King Xingguang of Silla died, and his son Chengqing succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen King Xingguang of Silla died, and his son Chengqing succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，幽州節度使張守珪破契丹-{於}-捺祿山。

translations.literal: On yiyou Zhang Shougui, military governor of Youzhou, defeated the Khitan at Nalushan.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Zhang Shougui, military governor of Youzhou, defeated the Khitan at Nalushan.

sentences.zh: 己亥，河西節度使崔希逸襲吐蕃，破之-{於}-靑海西。

translations.literal: On jihai Cui Xiyi, military governor of Hexi, raided the Tibetans and defeated them west of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Cui Xiyi, military governor of Hexi, raided the Tibetans and defeated them west of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 初，希逸遣使謂吐蕃邊將乞力徐曰：「兩國通好，今爲一家，何必更置兵守捉，妨人耕牧！

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiyi sent an envoy to tell the Tibetan frontier general Qili Xu: "Our two states are on good terms and are now one family—why must we still post troops to guard and seize, hindering men's plowing and herding!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiyi sent an envoy to tell the Tibetan frontier general Qili Xu, "Our two states are on good terms and are now one family—why must we still post troops to guard and seize, hindering men's plowing and herding!

sentences.zh: 請皆罷之。

translations.literal: I ask that we all withdraw them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we all withdraw them.

sentences.zh: 」乞力徐曰：「常侍忠厚，言必不欺。

translations.literal: " Qili Xu said: "The Regular Attendant is honest and generous; his words surely will not deceive.
translations.idiomatic: " Qili Xu said, "The Regular Attendant is honest and generous; his words surely will not deceive.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷未必專以邊事相委，萬一有-{奸}-人交-{斗}-其間，掩吾無備，悔之何及！

translations.literal: Yet the court may not entrust frontier affairs to you alone; should some villain stir strife between us and strike us unprepared, how can regret come in time!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court may not entrust frontier affairs to you alone; should some villain stir strife between us and strike us unprepared, how can regret come in time!

sentences.zh: 」希逸固請，乃刑白狗爲盟，各去守備；

translations.literal: " Xiyi pressed his request firmly, and so they slaughtered a white dog to seal the covenant and each withdrew his garrisons;
translations.idiomatic: " Xiyi pressed his request firmly, and so they slaughtered a white dog to seal the covenant and each withdrew his garrisons;

sentences.zh: -{於}-是吐蕃畜牧被野。

translations.literal: thereupon Tibetan herds and flocks spread across the wild.
translations.idiomatic: thereupon Tibetan herds and flocks spread across the wild.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃西撃勃律，勃律來告急。

translations.literal: At that time the Tibetans were striking Bolü in the west, and Bolü came to report urgency.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tibetans were striking Bolü in the west, and Bolü came to report urgency.

sentences.zh: 上命吐蕃罷兵，吐蕃不奉詔，遂破勃律；

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Tibetans to cease military action; the Tibetans did not obey the edict and thereupon destroyed Bolü;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the Tibetans to cease military action; the Tibetans did not obey the edict and thereupon destroyed Bolü;

sentences.zh: 上甚怒。

translations.literal: the Emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 會希逸傔人孫誨入奏事，自欲求功，奏稱吐蕃無備，請掩撃，必大獲。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiyi's attendant Sun Hui came in to report on affairs; wishing merit for himself, he memorialized that the Tibetans were unprepared and asked for a surprise attack, saying great gains were certain.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Xiyi's attendant Sun Hui came in to report on affairs; wishing merit for himself, he memorialized that the Tibetans were unprepared and asked for a surprise attack, saying great gains were certain.

sentences.zh: 上命内給事趙惠琮與誨偕往，審察事宜。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Inner Provisioner Zhao Huizong to go with Hui and examine the matter on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Inner Provisioner Zhao Huizong to go with Hui and examine the matter on the spot.

sentences.zh: 惠琮等至，則矯詔令希逸襲之。

translations.literal: When Huizong and the others arrived, they forged an edict ordering Xiyi to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong and the others arrived, they forged an edict ordering Xiyi to attack.

sentences.zh: 希逸不得已，-{發}-兵自涼州南入吐蕃境二千-{餘}--{里}-，至靑海西，與吐蕃戰，大破之，斬首二千-{餘}-級，乞力徐脱身走。

translations.literal: Xiyi had no choice; he raised troops from Liangzhou south into Tibetan territory more than two thousand li, reaching west of Qinghai, fought the Tibetans, and routed them greatly, beheading more than two thousand; Qili Xu escaped and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi had no choice; he raised troops from Liangzhou south into Tibetan territory more than two thousand li, reaching west of Qinghai, fought the Tibetans, and routed them greatly, beheading more than two thousand; Qili Xu escaped and fled.

sentences.zh: 惠琮、誨皆受厚賞。

translations.literal: Huizong and Hui both received rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong and Hui both received rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 自是吐蕃-{復}-絶朝貢。

translations.literal: From then on the Tibetans again cut off court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Tibetans again cut off court tribute.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛酉，監察-{御}-史周子諒彈牛仙客非-{才}-，引讖書爲證。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinyou Supervising Censor Zhou Ziliang impeached Niu Xianke as lacking talent and cited apocryphal texts as proof.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinyou Supervising Censor Zhou Ziliang impeached Niu Xianke as lacking talent and cited apocryphal texts as proof.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命左右手暴-{於}-殿庭，絶而-{復}-甦；

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and ordered the attendants to beat him bare-handed in the palace courtyard until he ceased breathing and then revived him;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and ordered the attendants to beat him bare-handed in the palace courtyard until he ceased breathing and then revived him;

sentences.zh: 仍杖之朝堂，流瀼州，至藍田而死。

translations.literal: he was still caned in the court hall, banished to Rang Prefecture, and died at Lantian on the way.
translations.idiomatic: he was still caned in the court hall, banished to Rang Prefecture, and died at Lantian on the way.

sentences.zh: 李林甫言：「子諒，張九齡所-{薦}-也。

translations.literal: Li Linfu said: "Ziliang was recommended by Zhang Jiuling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu said, "Ziliang was recommended by Zhang Jiuling.

sentences.zh: 」甲子，貶九齡荊州長史。

translations.literal: " On jiazi Zhang Jiuling was demoted to senior administrator of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiazi Zhang Jiuling was demoted to senior administrator of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楊洄又譖太子瑛、鄂王瑤、光王琚，-{雲}-與太子妃兄駙馬薛銹潛構異謀，上召宰相謀之。

translations.literal: Yang Hui again slandered Crown Prince Ying, Prince E Yao, and Prince Guang Ju, saying that with the crown prince's consort's elder brother, Imperial Son-in-law Xue Xiu, they were secretly plotting rebellion; the Emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hui again slandered Crown Prince Ying, Prince E Yao, and Prince Guang Ju, saying that with the crown prince's consort's elder brother, Imperial Son-in-law Xue Xiu, they were secretly plotting rebellion; the Emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 李林甫對曰：「此陛下家事，非臣等所宜豫。

translations.literal: Li Linfu replied: "This is Your Majesty's own family affair and is not what your servants ought to take part in.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu replied, "This is Your Majesty's own family affair and is not what your servants ought to take part in.

sentences.zh: 」上意乃決。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor's mind was then decided.

sentences.zh: 乙-{丑}-，使宦者宣-{制}--{於}-宮中，廢瑛、瑤、琚爲庶人，流銹-{於}-瀼州。

translations.literal: On yichou he sent eunuchs to proclaim the edict within the palace, deposed Ying, Yao, and Ju as commoners, and banished Xiu to Rang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he sent eunuchs to proclaim the edict within the palace, deposed Ying, Yao, and Ju as commoners, and banished Xiu to Rang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瑛、瑤、琚尋賜死城東驛，銹賜死-{於}-藍田。

translations.literal: Ying, Yao, and Ju were soon ordered to die at the eastern post station; Xiu was ordered to die at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Yao, and Ju were soon ordered to die at the eastern post station; Xiu was ordered to die at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 瑤、琚皆好學，有-{才}-識，死不以罪，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Yao and Ju both loved learning and had talent and insight; they died without guilt, and all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Ju both loved learning and had talent and insight; they died without guilt, and all regretted it.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，瑛舅家趙氏、妃家薛氏、瑤舅家皇甫氏，坐流貶者數十人，惟瑤妃家韋氏以妃賢得免。

translations.literal: On bingyin the Zhao clan of Ying's mother's family, the Xue clan of his consort's family, and the Huangfu clan of Yao's mother's family—several tens of persons were implicated and banished; only the Wei clan of Yao's consort's family was spared because the consort was virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Zhao clan of Ying's mother's family, the Xue clan of his consort's family, and the Huangfu clan of Yao's mother's family—several tens of persons were implicated and banished; only the Wei clan of Yao's consort's family was spared because the consort was virtuous.

sentences.zh: 五月，夷州刺史楊浚坐贓當死，上命杖之六十，流古州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Yang Jun, prefect of Yi Prefecture, was charged with corruption and deserved death; the Emperor ordered him caned sixty strokes and banished to Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yang Jun, prefect of Yi Prefecture, was charged with corruption and deserved death; the Emperor ordered him caned sixty strokes and banished to Gu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 左丞相裴耀卿上疎，以爲：「決杖贖死，恩則甚優；

translations.literal: Left Chief Minister Pei Yaoji submitted a memorial, holding that: "Deciding death by the staff is merciful in the extreme as grace;
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Minister Pei Yaoji submitted a memorial, holding that, "Deciding death by the staff is merciful in the extreme as grace;

sentences.zh: 解體受笞，事頗爲辱，上可施之徒隸，不當及-{於}-士人。

translations.literal: to bare the body and receive beating is in the matter quite a disgrace; it may be applied to convict laborers above, but ought not extend to gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: to bare the body and receive beating is in the matter quite a disgrace; it may be applied to convict laborers above, but ought not extend to gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 癸未，敕以方隅底定，令中書門下與諸道節度使量軍鎭閒劇利害，審計兵防定額，-{於}-諸色-{-{徴}-}-人及客戸中召募丁壯，長充邊軍，增給田宅，務加優恤。

translations.literal: On guiwei an edict, because the four quarters were settled at the base, ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery together with the military governors of the various circuits to measure the busyness and ease and benefit and harm of the army garrisons, carefully calculate fixed quotas for frontier defense troops, and from among persons of various tax categories and guest households recruit able-bodied men to serve long as frontier soldiers, increasing grants of fields and dwellings and striving to add generous care.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei an edict, because the four quarters were settled at the base, ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery together with the military governors of the various circuits to measure the busyness and ease and benefit and harm of the army garrisons, carefully calculate fixed quotas for frontier defense troops, and from among persons of various tax categories and guest households recruit able-bodied men to serve long as frontier soldiers, increasing grants of fields and dwellings and striving to add generous care.

sentences.zh: 辛-{丑}-，上命有司選宗子有-{才}-者，授以-{台}-省及法官、京縣官，敕曰：「違道慢常，義無私-{於}-王法；

translations.literal: On xinchou the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to select talented clansmen of the imperial house and appoint them to terrace offices, judicial posts, and capital county offices; an edict said: "Those who violate the Way and slight constant norms have, in principle, no private claim upon royal law;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to select talented clansmen of the imperial house and appoint them to terrace offices, judicial posts, and capital county offices; an edict said, "Those who violate the Way and slight constant norms have, in principle, no private claim upon royal law;

sentences.zh: 修身效節，恩豈薄-{於}-它人！

translations.literal: those who cultivate the person and offer loyalty—how can favor be thinner than for others!
translations.idiomatic: those who cultivate the person and offer loyalty—how can favor be thinner than for others!

sentences.zh: 期-{於}-帥先，勵我風俗。

translations.literal: I look to you to lead first and encourage our customs.
translations.idiomatic: I look to you to lead first and encourage our customs.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己卯，大理少卿徐嶠奏：「今歳天下斷死刑五十八，大理獄院，由來相傳殺氣太盛，鳥雀不棲，今有鵲巣其樹。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jimao Senior Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Qiao memorialized: "This year executions under death sentence throughout the realm number fifty-eight. In the prison courtyard of the Court of Judicial Review it has been handed down that the killing qi is too strong and birds and sparrows do not roost; now magpies have nested in its trees.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jimao Senior Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Qiao memorialized, "This year executions under death sentence throughout the realm number fifty-eight. In the prison courtyard of the Court of Judicial Review it has been handed down that the killing qi is too strong and birds and sparrows do not roost; now magpies have nested in its trees.

sentences.zh: 」-{於}-是百官以-{幾}-致刑措，上表稱賀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the hundred officials, because punishments were nearly abolished, submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the hundred officials, because punishments were nearly abolished, submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 上歸功宰輔，庚辰，賜李林甫爵晉國公，牛仙客豳國公。

translations.literal: The Emperor attributed the merit to the chief ministers; on gengchen he granted Li Linfu the title Duke of Jin and Niu Xianke the title Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor attributed the merit to the chief ministers; on gengchen he granted Li Linfu the title Duke of Jin and Niu Xianke the title Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 上命李林甫、牛仙客與法官刪修《律令格式》成，九月，壬申，頒行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Li Linfu, Niu Xianke, and the judicial officials to revise and complete the Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms; in the ninth month, on renshen, they were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Li Linfu, Niu Xianke, and the judicial officials to revise and complete the Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and Forms; in the ninth month, on renshen, they were promulgated.

sentences.zh: 先是，西北邊數十州多宿重兵，地租營田皆不以贍，始用和糴之法。

translations.literal: Previously, on the northwest frontier dozens of prefectures had long stationed heavy troops; land rent and garrison-farm yields were insufficient to support them, and the method of harmonious grain purchase was first adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, along the northwest frontier dozens of prefectures had long kept large garrisons; local rents and military farm yields could not sustain them, and the government began buying grain at fair prices to make up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 有彭果者，因牛仙客獻策，請行糴法-{於}-關中。

translations.literal: There was one Peng Guo who, through Niu Xianke's presenting a plan, requested implementing the purchase law in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Peng Guo, acting through Niu Xianke, proposed extending the grain-purchase system to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 戊子，敕以歳稔-{谷}-賤傷農，命增時-{價}-什二三，和糴東、西畿粟各數百萬斛，停今年江、淮所運租。

translations.literal: On wuzi, an edict [said] that because the year was abundant grain was cheap and farmers were harmed, ordered raising the timely price by two or three tenths, harmoniously purchasing several million hu of grain in the eastern and western metropolitan circuits, and halting this year's grain rents transported from the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi an edict declared that the bumper harvest had driven grain prices so low as to hurt farmers; the court ordered prices raised by twenty or thirty percent, procured several million hu in the eastern and western capital circuits, and suspended this year's Jiang-Huai grain shipments.

sentences.zh: 自是關中蓄積羨溢，車駕不-{復}-幸東都矣。

translations.literal: From then on Guanzhong's stored grain overflowed, and the imperial carriage no longer visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Guanzhong's granaries overflowed, and the Emperor never again traveled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，敕河南、北租應輸含嘉、太原倉者，皆留輸本州。

translations.literal: On guisi, an edict [said] that Henan and Hebei rents that should be delivered to Hanjia and Taiyuan granaries would all be retained and delivered to their home prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi an edict ordered that Henan and Hebei rents bound for the Hanjia and Taiyuan granaries should instead be kept and delivered within their home prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王璵上疎請立靑帝壇以迎春；

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Wang Yu submitted a memorial requesting establishment of an Azure Emperor altar to welcome spring;
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Yu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized asking that an altar to the Azure Emperor be built for the spring welcoming rite;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The Emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛-{丑}-，-{制}-自今立春親迎春-{於}-東郊。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, an edict [said] that from now on at the Beginning of Spring [the Emperor] would personally welcome spring in the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, an edict ordered that from then on the Emperor would personally welcome spring at the eastern suburb on the day the season began.

sentences.zh: 時上頗好祀神鬼，故璵專習祠祭之禮以-{干}-時。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor rather favored sacrificing to spirits and ghosts, so Yu specialized in studying sacrifice ritual to win the times.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had grown fond of worshiping spirits and ghosts, so Yu devoted himself to sacrificial ritual to win favor.

sentences.zh: 上悅之，以爲侍-{御}-史，領祠祭使。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased with him and made him Attending Censor, in charge of the Sacrifice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased with him, the Emperor made him an Attending Censor and put him in charge of sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 璵祈禱或焚紙錢，類巫覡，習禮者羞之。

translations.literal: When Yu prayed he sometimes burned paper money, resembling shamans; those versed in ritual were ashamed of this.
translations.idiomatic: In his prayers Yu sometimes burned paper money like a shaman, to the embarrassment of ritual specialists.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上幸驪山温泉。

translations.literal: On renshen the Emperor visited Mount Li hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，還宮。

translations.literal: On yiyou he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 己-{丑}-，開府儀同三司廣平文貞公宋璟薨。

translations.literal: On jichou Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equal Ceremony Under Three Excellencies Duke Wen and Pure of Guangping Song Jing died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Song Jing, Duke Wen and Pure of Guangping, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equal Ceremony Under Three Excellencies, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙午，惠妃武氏薨，贈謚貞順皇-{后}-。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, Huifei of the Wu clan died; posthumously she was granted the title Empress Zhenshun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingwu, Consort Wu Huifei died and was posthumously honored as Empress Zhenshun.

sentences.zh: 是歳，命將作大匠康愆素之東都毀明堂。

translations.literal: That year the Emperor ordered Master of Palace Works Kang Qiansu to go to the Eastern Capital to destroy the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That year he ordered Master of Palace Works Kang Qiansu to go to Luoyang and dismantle the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 愆素上言：「毀之勞人，請去上層，卑-{於}-舊九十五尺，仍舊爲-{乾}-元殿。

translations.literal: Qiansu memorialized: "Destroying it would weary the people; I request removing the upper story, making it ninety-five chi lower than the old [height], and restoring it as the Hall of Primordial Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Kang Qiansu memorialized: "Tearing it down would exhaust the people. I ask that only the upper story be removed, the height lowered ninety-five chi below the old measure, and the building restored as the Hall of Primordial Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: [The Emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 初令庸調租資課皆以土物輸京都。

translations.literal: For the first time it was ordered that corvée, land tax, and miscellaneous levies all be submitted to the capital in local products.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time corvée, land tax, and miscellaneous levies were all required to be paid to the capital in local goods rather than cash.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，以牛仙客爲侍中。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Niu Xianke was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Niu Xianke was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁-{丑}-，上迎氣-{於}-滻水之東。

translations.literal: On dingchou the Emperor welcomed the qi at the east of the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Emperor performed the seasonal qi rite east of the Chan River.

sentences.zh: -{制}-邊地長-{-{徴}-}-兵，召募向足，自今鎭兵勿-{復}-遣，在彼者縱還。

translations.literal: An edict [said]: border regions had for years levied troops; recruitment is now sufficient; from now on do not again dispatch garrison troops [from the interior]; those already there may return home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that the border circuits had long levied troops but recruitment was now sufficient; henceforth interior garrisons were not to be sent out again, and men already stationed on the frontier might go home.

sentences.zh: 令天下州、縣、裡別置學。

translations.literal: It was ordered that throughout the realm prefectures, counties, and village wards each establish schools separately.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered every prefecture, county, and village ward in the empire to establish its own school.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以李林甫領隴右節度副大使，以鄯州都督杜希望知留-{後}-。

translations.literal: On renchen Li Linfu was made associate military commissioner of Longyou Circuit, and Shazhou military governor Du Xiwang was made acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Li Linfu was made associate commissioner of Longyou Circuit, and Shazhou military governor Du Xiwang was left in charge as acting regent.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯，以牛仙客兼河東節度副大使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yimao, Niu Xianke was also made associate military commissioner of Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao, Niu Xianke was also made associate commissioner of Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 己未，葬貞順皇-{后}--{於}-敬陵。

translations.literal: On jiwei the Empress Zhenshun was buried at Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Empress Zhenshun was buried at Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，敕河-{曲}-六州胡坐康待賓散隸諸州者，-{聽}-還故土，-{於}-鹽、夏之間，置宥州以處之。

translations.literal: On renxu an edict [said] that Hu of the six prefectures on the River Bend who had been scattered after Kang Daibin's sit-in and assigned to various prefectures might return to their former lands; between Yan and Xia a You Prefecture would be established to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu an edict allowed the River Bend Hu, scattered among the prefectures after Kang Daibin's rebellion, to return to their homelands; a You Prefecture was established between Yan and Xia to receive them.

sentences.zh: 三月，吐蕃寇河西，節度使崔希逸撃破之。

translations.literal: In the third month Tibet raided Hexi; military governor Cui Xiyi defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Tibet raided Hexi; military governor Cui Xiyi drove them back.

sentences.zh: 鄯州都督、知隴右留-{後}-杜希望攻吐蕃新城，拔之，以其地爲威戎軍，置兵一千戍之。

translations.literal: Shazhou military governor and acting Longyou regent Du Xiwang attacked Tibet's New City, took it, made the place Weirong Army, and stationed one thousand troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiwang, military governor of Shazhou and acting regent of Longyou, stormed Tibet's New City, took it, made it Weirong Army, and left a garrison of one thousand men.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙酉，李林甫兼河西節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yiyou, Li Linfu was also made military governor of Hexi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on yiyou, Li Linfu was also made military governor of Hexi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以崔希逸爲河南尹。

translations.literal: On bingshen Cui Xiyi was made Henan Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Cui Xiyi was appointed Henan Intendant.

sentences.zh: 希逸自念失信-{於}-吐蕃，内懷愧恨，未-{幾}-而卒。

translations.literal: Xiyi himself reflected that he had broken faith with Tibet and harbored shame and resentment; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi brooded over having betrayed Tibet; consumed by shame, he died not long after.

sentences.zh: 太子瑛既死，李林甫數勸上立壽王瑁。

translations.literal: After Crown Prince Ying had died, Li Linfu repeatedly urged the Emperor to establish Prince Shou Mao.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Ying's death, Li Linfu repeatedly urged the Emperor to make Prince Shou Li Mao heir.

sentences.zh: 上以忠王璵年長，且仁孝恭謹，又好學，意欲立之，猶豫歳-{餘}-不決。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Prince of Zhong Yu was the eldest and moreover filial, reverent, and careful, and also fond of learning, intended to establish him, but hesitated for more than a year without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor favored Prince of Zhong Li Yu as the eldest son—filial, reverent, studious—and meant to name him heir, yet hesitated for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 自念春秋浸髙，三子同日誅死，繼嗣未定，常忽忽不樂，寢膳爲之減。

translations.literal: Reflecting that his years were gradually advancing, three sons executed on the same day, the succession unsettled, he was constantly restless and unhappy, and his sleep and meals diminished on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: He brooded on his advancing age, on three sons executed in a single day, and on an unsettled succession; he grew restless and joyless, and even sleep and appetite failed him.

sentences.zh: 髙力士乘間請其故，上曰：「汝，我家老奴，豈不能揣我意！

translations.literal: Gao Lishi seized an opening to ask the reason; the Emperor said, "You are my family's old slave—can you not divine my mind!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi seized a quiet moment to ask what troubled him. The Emperor said, "You are the old slave of my house—can you not read my mind!

sentences.zh: 」力士曰：「得非以郎君未定邪？

translations.literal: Lishi said, "Is it not because the heir is not yet settled?"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said, "Is it not because the heir is still undecided?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「大家何必如此虚勞聖心，但推長而立，誰敢-{復}-爭！

translations.literal: He replied, "Why must Your Majesty so vainly weary your sacred heart? Simply establish the eldest—who would dare contend again!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Why weary yourself so? Simply install the eldest—who would dare dispute it!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「汝言是也！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Your words are right!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You are right!"

sentences.zh: 汝言是也！

translations.literal: Your words are right!
translations.idiomatic: You are right!

sentences.zh: 」由是遂定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: And so the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，立璵爲太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Yu was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Li Yu was installed as Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 辛-{丑}-，以岐州刺史蕭炅爲河西節度使總留-{後}-事，鄯州都督杜希望爲隴右節度使，太-{僕}-卿王昱爲劍南節度使，分道經略吐蕃，仍毀所立赤嶺碑。

translations.literal: On xinchou Qizhou prefect Xiao Jiong was made military governor of Hexi Circuit overseeing the regent's affairs; Shazhou military governor Du Xiwang was made military governor of Longyou Circuit; Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Wang Yu was made military governor of Jiannan Circuit; they would advance by separate routes against Tibet, and still destroy the Red Ridge stele that had been erected.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Xiao Jiong, prefect of Qizhou, was made military governor of Hexi with overall charge; Du Xiwang became military governor of Longyou; Wang Yu, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, was sent to Jiannan; each was to strike Tibet by a separate route and tear down the Red Ridge treaty stele.

sentences.zh: 突騎施可汗功祿，素廉儉，毎攻戰所得，輒與諸部分之，不留私蓄，由是衆樂爲用。

translations.literal: Turgesh Khan Gonglu was by nature frugal; whenever he gained booty in battle he at once divided it among the tribes, leaving no private stores; for this the masses were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: The Turgesh khan Suluo was frugal by nature; after every battle he divided the spoils among his tribes and kept nothing for himself, and his people gladly followed him.

sentences.zh: 既尚唐公主，又潛通突厥及吐蕃，突厥、吐蕃各以女妻之。

translations.literal: Having married a Tang princess, he also secretly communicated with the Turks and Tibet; the Turks and Tibet each gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had married a Tang princess, he also dealt secretly with the Turks and Tibet, and each realm gave him a wife.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿以三國女爲可敦，又立數子爲-{葉}-護，用度浸廣，由是攻戰所得，不-{復}-更分。

translations.literal: Sulu took women of the three states as khatuns and also established several sons as yabghus; expenses gradually broadened, and from then on battle gains were no longer redistributed.
translations.idiomatic: Suluo took wives from all three powers as khatuns and made several sons yabghus; expenses mounted, and he no longer shared the spoils of war.

sentences.zh: 晩年病風，一手攣縮，諸部離心。

translations.literal: In his later years he fell ill with wind disease; one hand curled and shrank, and the tribes lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he suffered a paralytic stroke; one hand curled useless, and the tribes lost heart.

sentences.zh: 酋長莫賀達-{干}-、都摩度兩部最強，其部落又分爲黃姓、黑姓，互相乖阻，-{於}-是莫賀達-{干}-勒兵夜襲蘇祿，殺之。

translations.literal: Chiefs Mohedagan and Dumedu were the two strongest divisions; their tribes further split into Yellow Surname and Black Surname, each obstructing the other; thereupon Mohedagan led troops by night to surprise Sulu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs Mohedagan and Dumedu were the strongest factions; their people further split into Yellow and Black surnames at odds with one another. Mohedagan then led a night attack on Suluo and killed him.

sentences.zh: 都摩度初與莫賀達-{干}-連謀，既而-{復}-與之異，立蘇祿之子骨啜爲吐火仙可汗，以收其-{餘}-衆，與莫賀達-{干}-相攻。

translations.literal: Dumedu at first joined Mohedagan in conspiracy, but then again differed from him; he established Sulu's son Guchuo as Tuhuoxian Khan to gather the remaining followers, and they attacked each other.
translations.idiomatic: Dumedu had first plotted with Mohedagan, then turned against him; he set up Suluo's son Guchuo as Khan Tuhuoxian to rally the remnants, and the two factions warred on each other.

sentences.zh: 莫賀達-{干}-遣使告磧西節度使蓋嘉運，上命嘉運招集突騎施、拔汗那以西諸國；

translations.literal: Mohedagan sent envoys to inform Beiting military governor Gai Jiayun; the Emperor ordered Jiayun to summon and assemble Turgesh, Fergana, and the states west of them;
translations.idiomatic: Mohedagan sent envoys to Beiting military governor Gai Jiayun; the Emperor ordered Jiayun to rally Turgesh, Fergana, and the states beyond.

sentences.zh: 吐火仙與都摩度據碎-{葉}-城，黑姓可汗爾微特勒據怛邏斯城，相與連兵以拒唐。

translations.literal: Tuhuoxian and Dumedu held Suyab city; Black Surname Khan Erwei Tele held Talas city; they joined forces to resist Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhuoxian and Dumedu held Suyab; the Black Surname khan Erwei Tele held Talas; together they raised arms against Tang.

sentences.zh: 太子將受冊命，儀注有中嚴、外辦及絳紗袍，太子嫌與至尊同稱，表請易之。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was to receive the investiture, the ceremonial regulations included inner stern guard, outer preparation, and crimson gauze robe; the Crown Prince disliked sharing titles with the Sovereign and memorialized requesting changes.
translations.idiomatic: As the Crown Prince's investiture neared, the ritual code gave him an inner stern guard, an outer preparation, and a crimson gauze robe—titles too close to the Emperor's. He memorialized asking that they be changed.

sentences.zh: 左丞相裴耀卿奏停中嚴，改外辦曰外備，改絳紗袍爲朱明服。

translations.literal: Left Chief Minister Pei Yaoqing memorialized to stop the inner stern guard, change outer preparation to outer reserve, and change the crimson gauze robe to vermilion-bright attire.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Minister Pei Yaoqing memorialized to abolish the inner stern guard, rename outer preparation as outer reserve, and replace the crimson gauze robe with vermilion-bright attire.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己巳，上-{御}-宣政殿，冊太子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jisi, the Emperor ascended Xuanzheng Hall and invested the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jisi, the Emperor took the throne at Xuanzheng Hall and invested the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 故事，太子乘輅至殿門。

translations.literal: By precedent the Crown Prince rode the imperial carriage to the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Crown Prince rode the imperial carriage to the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 至是，太子不就輅，自其宮歩入。

translations.literal: On this occasion the Crown Prince did not take the carriage but walked from his palace.
translations.idiomatic: This time he refused the carriage and walked from his own palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，赦天下。

translations.literal: That day there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That day a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 己卯，冊忠王妃韋氏爲太子妃。

translations.literal: On jimao the Consort of Prince of Zhong of the Wei clan was invested as Crown Princess.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the consort of Prince of Zhong, of the Wei clan, was invested as Crown Princess.

sentences.zh: 杜希望將鄯州之衆奪吐蕃河橋，-{築}-鹽泉城-{於}-河左，吐蕃-{發}-兵三萬逆戰，希望衆少，不敵，將卒皆懼。

translations.literal: Du Xiwang led the Shazhou forces to seize Tibet's river bridge, built Yancheng Fort on the river's left; Tibet sent thirty thousand troops to meet them in battle; Xiwang's force was few and could not match them; officers and soldiers were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiwang led the Shazhou army to seize Tibet's river bridge and built Salt Spring Fort on the left bank. Tibet sent thirty thousand men to meet him; Xiwang's force was too small, and his officers and men were afraid.

sentences.zh: 左威衞郎將王忠嗣帥所部先犯其陳，所向-{辟}-易，殺數百人，虜陳亂。

translations.literal: Left Majestic Guard commandant Wang Zhongsi led his unit to strike their formation first; wherever he went they yielded; he killed several hundred, and the barbarian formation was thrown into confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Left Majestic Guard commandant Wang Zhongsi led his men in the first charge; wherever he struck the enemy gave way; he killed several hundred and threw their line into disorder.

sentences.zh: 希望縱兵乘之，虜遂大敗。

translations.literal: Xiwang unleashed his troops to follow up, and the barbarians were thoroughly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwang then threw his whole force forward, and the Tibetans were routed.

sentences.zh: 置鎭西軍-{於}-鹽泉。

translations.literal: Zhenxi Army was established at Yanquan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenxi Army was established at Salt Spring.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣以功遷左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Zhongsi for his merit was promoted to General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Wang Zhongsi was promoted to general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛巳，勃海王武藝卒，子欽茂立。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinsi, Bohai King Wu Yi's died; his son Qinmao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinsi, Bohai King Wu Yi died; his son Qinmao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingshen the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingshen, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 初，儀鳳中，吐蕃陷安戎城而據之，其地險要，唐屢攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Previously, in the Yifeng era, Tibet had taken Anyong City and held it; the terrain was perilous, and Tang repeatedly attacked without success.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Yifeng era, Tibet had taken Anyong City and held its commanding ground; Tang attacked again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 劍南節度使王昱-{築}-兩城-{於}-其側，頓軍蒲婆嶺下，運資糧以逼之。

translations.literal: Jiannan military governor Wang Yu built two forts at its flank, encamped troops below Pupoling, and transported provisions to press upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan military governor Wang Yu built two forts beside it, camped at Pupoling, and pushed supplies forward to starve the garrison out.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大-{發}-兵救安戎城，昱衆大敗，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Tibet sent a great force to rescue Anyong City; Yu's army was thoroughly defeated, and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent a great army to relieve the city; Wang Yu's force was shattered and several thousand men died.

sentences.zh: 昱脱身走，糧仗軍資皆棄之。

translations.literal: Yu himself escaped; grain, weapons, and military stores were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu himself fled, abandoning grain, arms, and all military stores.

sentences.zh: 貶昱括州刺史，再貶髙要尉而死。

translations.literal: He was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou, then demoted again to defender of Gaoyao and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou, then again to defender of Gaoyao, where he died.

sentences.zh: 戊午，冊南詔蒙歸義爲-{雲}-南王。

translations.literal: On wuwu Nan Zhao Meng Guiyi was invested as King of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Meng Guiyi of Nan Zhao was invested as King of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 歸義之先本哀牢夷，地居姚州之西，東南接交趾，西北接吐蕃。

translations.literal: Guiyi's ancestors were originally Ailao Yi; their land lay west of Yaozhou, southeast joining Jiaozhi, northwest joining Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyi's people were originally Ailao Yi, living west of Yaozhou, with Jiaozhi to the southeast and Tibet to the northwest.

sentences.zh: 蠻語謂王曰詔，先有六詔：曰蒙-{捨}-，曰蒙越，曰越析，曰浪穹，曰樣備，曰越澹，兵力相埒，莫能相壹；

translations.literal: In the barbarian tongue king is called zhao; there were first six zhao: called Mengshe, Mengyue, Yuexi, Langqiong, Yangbei, Yuetan; military strength was equal, none could unite the rest;
translations.idiomatic: In their tongue a king was called zhao. Six zhao had long existed—Mengshe, Mengyue, Yuexi, Langqiong, Yangbei, and Yuetan—each with comparable strength and none able to subdue the rest;

sentences.zh: 歴代因之以分其勢。

translations.literal: successive dynasties relied on this to divide their power.
translations.idiomatic: successive dynasties had relied on that division to keep them weak.

sentences.zh: 蒙-{捨}-最在南，故謂之南詔。

translations.literal: Mengshe was southernmost, hence called Nan Zhao (Southern Zhao).
translations.idiomatic: Mengshe lay farthest south, hence the name Nan Zhao, Southern Zhao.

sentences.zh: 髙宗時，蒙-{捨}-細奴邏初入朝。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong era Mengshe Xinuoluo first entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozong's reign Xinuoluo of Mengshe first came to court.

sentences.zh: 細奴邏生邏盛，邏盛生盛邏皮，盛邏皮生皮邏閣。

translations.literal: Xinuoluo begot Luosheng; Luosheng begot Shengluopi; Shengluopi begot Piluoge.
translations.idiomatic: Xinuoluo was succeeded by Luosheng, then Shengluopi, then Piluoge.

sentences.zh: 皮邏閣浸強大，而五詔微弱；

translations.literal: Piluoge gradually grew powerful while the five zhao grew weak;
translations.idiomatic: Piluoge grew steadily stronger while the other five zhao weakened;

sentences.zh: 會有破渳河蠻之功，乃賂王昱，求合六詔爲一。

translations.literal: when he had merit in defeating the Mishe River barbarians, he bribed Wang Yu, requesting to unite the six zhao into one.
translations.idiomatic: after defeating the Mishe River tribes he bribed Wang Yu to petition that the six zhao be united under one rule.

sentences.zh: 昱爲之奏請，朝遷許之，仍賜名歸義。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized on his behalf; the court granted it and additionally bestowed the name Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu memorialized on his behalf; the court agreed and bestowed the name Guiyi.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是以兵威脅服群蠻，不從者滅之，遂撃破吐蕃，徙居大和城；

translations.literal: Thereupon by military might he compelled the various barbarians; those who did not submit he destroyed, and he also defeated Tibet and moved his seat to Dali City;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he cowed the other tribes by force, destroyed those who refused submission, defeated Tibet, and moved his seat to Dali;

sentences.zh: 其-{後}-卒爲邊患。

translations.literal: afterward he would become a frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: and in time he became a scourge on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，上幸驪山温泉，壬辰，上還宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin the Emperor visited Mount Li hot springs; on renchen he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin the Emperor visited the Mount Li hot springs; on renchen he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 是歳，-{於}-西京、東都往來之路，作行宮千-{餘}-間。

translations.literal: That year, on the road between the Western and Eastern capitals, more than a thousand traveling palaces were built.
translations.idiomatic: That year more than a thousand way stations were built along the road between Chang'an and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 分左右羽林置龍武軍，以萬騎營隸焉。

translations.literal: Left and right Winged Forest Armies established the Dragon Martial Army, subordinating the Ten Thousand Riders camp to it.
translations.idiomatic: From the left and right Winged Forest Armies the Dragon Martial Army was formed, with the Ten Thousand Riders camp placed under it.

sentences.zh: 潤州刺史齊澣奏：「舊自瓜歩濟江，迂六十-{里}-。

translations.literal: Runzhou prefect Qi Huan memorialized: "Formerly from Guabu one crossed the Yangtze, a detour of sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: Runzhou prefect Qi Huan memorialized: "The old route from Guabu crossed the Yangtze by a sixty-li detour.

sentences.zh: 請自京口埭下直濟江，穿伊婁河二十五-{里}-即達揚子縣，立伊婁埭。

translations.literal: I request from below the Jingkou dam going straight across the Yangtze, cutting through the Yilou River twenty-five li to reach Yangzi County, and establishing the Yilou dam."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a channel be opened from below the Jingkou dam straight across the river, cutting the Yilou River for twenty-five li to reach Yangzi County, with a new Yilou dam built there."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: [The Emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，命隴右節度大使榮王琬自至本道巡按處置諸軍，選募關内、河東壯士三五萬人，詣隴右防遏，至秋末無寇，-{聽}-還。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renyin the Emperor ordered Longyou military commissioner Prince of Rong Wan to proceed in person to that circuit to inspect and dispose the various armies, select and recruit thirty to fifty thousand strong men from Guannei and Hedong, send them to Longyou to block the enemy; if by autumn's end there were no raiders, they were permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renyin the Emperor ordered Prince of Rong Li Wan, commissioner of Longyou, to tour his circuit in person, inspect the armies, and recruit thirty to fifty thousand stalwarts from Guannei and Hedong to reinforce Longyou; if no enemy appeared by autumn's end, they might go home.

sentences.zh: 群臣請加尊號曰聖文；

translations.literal: The hundred officials requested adding an honorific title reading Sacred Culture;
translations.idiomatic: The officials asked that the honorific Sacred Culture be added to his title;

sentences.zh: 二月，己巳，許之，因赦天下，免百姓今年田租。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jisi [the Emperor] granted it; thereupon he amnestied all under Heaven and exempted the common people from this year's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month, on jisi, he assented, amnestied the realm, and remitted the year's land tax.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸酉，敕：「諸陰陽-{術}-數，自非婚喪-{卜}-擇，皆禁之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guiyou, an edict [said]: "All yin-yang arts and numerology, except for marriage and funeral divination and selection, are all forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiyou, an edict declared: "All occult arts and divination, except for wedding and funeral augury, are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 己-{丑}-，以牛仙客爲兵部尚書兼侍中，李林甫爲吏部尚書兼中書令，總文武選事。

translations.literal: On jichou Niu Xianke was made Minister of War with concurrent status as Palace Attendant, and Li Linfu was made Minister of Personnel with concurrent status as Director of the Secretariat; together they oversaw civil and military selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Niu Xianke was made Minister of War and Palace Attendant, and Li Linfu Minister of Personnel and Director of the Secretariat; together they took charge of civil and military appointments.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸酉，以-{御}-史大夫李-{適}-之兼幽州節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guiyou Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi was also made military governor of Youzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiyou Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi was also made military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 幽州將趙堪、白眞阤羅矯節度使張守珪之命，使平盧軍使烏知義邀撃叛奚-{餘}-黨-{於}-橫水之北；

translations.literal: Youzhou generals Zhao Kan and Bai Zhentuoluo forged military governor Zhang Shougui's orders, making Pinglu army commander Wu Zhiyi intercept remaining rebel Xi clans north of Hengshui;
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou generals Zhao Kan and Bai Zhentuoluo forged orders in Zhang Shougui's name directing Pinglu commander Wu Zhiyi to strike remnant Xi rebels north of Hengshui;

sentences.zh: 知義不從，白眞阤羅矯稱-{制}-指以迫之。

translations.literal: Zhiyi would not comply; Bai Zhentuoluo forged an imperial directive to compel him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi refused; Bai Zhentuoluo then forged an imperial directive to force him out.

sentences.zh: 知義不得已出師，與虜遇，先勝-{後}-敗；

translations.literal: Zhiyi had no choice but to take the field; he encountered the barbarians, first victorious then defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi had no choice but to march; he met the enemy, won at first, then lost;

sentences.zh: 守珪隱其敗狀，以克獲聞。

translations.literal: Shougui concealed the defeat and reported it as a capture and victory.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui hid the defeat and reported a victory.

sentences.zh: 事頗洩，上令内謁者監牛仙童作察之。

translations.literal: The matter leaked considerably; the Emperor ordered Palace Insider Supervisor Niu Xiantong to investigate it.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the affair spread; the Emperor sent Palace Insider Supervisor Niu Xiantong to look into it.

sentences.zh: 守珪重賂仙童，歸罪-{於}-白眞阤羅，逼令自縊死。

translations.literal: Shougui bribed Xiantong heavily, shifted the blame onto Bai Zhentuoluo, and compelled him to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui paid Xiantong a heavy bribe, pinned the crime on Bai Zhentuoluo, and forced him to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 仙童有寵-{於}-上，衆宦官疾之，共-{發}-其事。

translations.literal: Xiantong was favored by the Emperor; the eunuchs envied him and jointly exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xiantong enjoyed the Emperor's favor; the other eunuchs resented him and together brought the matter to light.

sentences.zh: 上怒，甲戌，命楊思勗杖殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged; on jiaxu he ordered Yang Si'en to beat him to death with the cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage; on jiaxu he ordered Yang Si'en to club him to death.

sentences.zh: 思勗縛格，杖之數百，刳取其心，割其肉啖之。

translations.literal: Si'en bound him fast, beat him hundreds of times, gouged out his heart, and cut his flesh to eat it.
translations.idiomatic: Si'en trussed him up, beat him hundreds of strokes, cut out his heart, and ate his flesh.

sentences.zh: 守珪坐貶括州刺史。

translations.literal: Shougui was punished by demotion to prefect of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 太子太師蕭-{嵩}-嘗賂仙童以城南良田數頃，李林甫-{發}-之，-{嵩}-坐貶靑州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor of the Heir Xiao Song had once bribed Xiantong with several qing of fine fields south of the city; Li Linfu exposed it, and Song was punished with demotion to prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor of the Heir Xiao Song had once given Xiantong several qing of fine land south of the capital; Li Linfu exposed him, and Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙亥，磧西節度使蓋嘉運擒突騎施可汗吐火仙。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yihai, Qixi military governor Gai Jiayun captured Turgesh qaghan Tuhuoxian.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yihai, Qixi military governor Gai Jiayun took the Turgesh qaghan Tuhuoxian prisoner.

sentences.zh: 嘉運攻碎-{葉}-城，吐火仙出戰，敗走，擒之-{於}-賀邏嶺。

translations.literal: Jiayun attacked Suyab; Tuhuoxian came out to fight, was defeated and fled, and was captured at Helu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun assaulted Suyab; Tuhuoxian marched out, was beaten and fled, and was seized at Helu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 分遣疎勒鎭守使夫蒙靈察與拔汗那王阿悉爛達-{干}-潛引兵突入怛邏斯城，擒黑姓可汗爾微，遂入曳建城，取交河公主，悉收散-{發}-之民數萬以與拔汗那王，威震西陲。

translations.literal: He separately dispatched Khotan garrison commissioner Fumeng Lingcha and the king of Ferghana, Ashilan Mohedagan, to lead troops by stealth into Talas city, capture the Black-clan qaghan Erwei, then enter Yejian city, take the Princess of Jiaohe, and gather all the scattered people numbering tens of thousands to give to the king of Ferghana; his might shook the western marches.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Khotan commissioner Fumeng Lingcha and Ferghana's king Ashilan Mohedagan to steal into Talas, seize Black-clan qaghan Erwei, enter Yejian, recover the Princess of Jiaohe, and rally tens of thousands of scattered subjects for the Ferghana king—his fame thundered across the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 壬午，吐蕃寇白草、安人等軍，隴右節度使蕭炅撃破之。

translations.literal: On renwu Tibet raided the armies of Baicao and Anren; Longyou military governor Xiao Jiong defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Tibet attacked the Baicao and Anren garrisons; Longyou military governor Xiao Jiong drove them off.

sentences.zh: 甲申，追謚孔子爲文宣王。

translations.literal: On jiashen Confucius was posthumously ennobled as King Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Confucius was posthumously titled King Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，祀先聖先師，周公南向，孔子東向坐。

translations.literal: Previously, in sacrificing to the Former Sage and Former Teacher, the Duke of Zhou faced south and Confucius sat facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when sacrificing to the Former Sage and Former Teacher, the Duke of Zhou faced south and Confucius sat facing east.

sentences.zh: -{制}-：「自今孔子南向坐，被王者之服，釋奠用宮懸。

translations.literal: An edict [said]: "From now on Confucius shall sit facing south, wear the robes of a king, and the libation sacrifice shall employ the full palace orchestra.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Henceforth Confucius shall face south, wear a king's robes, and the libation sacrifice shall use the full palace orchestra.

sentences.zh: 」追贈弟子皆爲公、侯、伯。

translations.literal: " His disciples were posthumously endowed with ranks of duke, marquis, and earl.
translations.idiomatic: " His disciples were posthumously given ranks of duke, marquis, and earl.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊午，處木昆、鼠尼施、弓月等諸部先隸突騎施者，皆帥衆内附，仍請徙居安西管内。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuwu, the tribes Chumukun, Shunishi, Gongyue, and others formerly subject to Turgesh all led their people to submit inward and still requested relocation within the Anxi protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuwu, the Chumukun, Shunishi, Gongyue, and other tribes once under Turgesh all led their clans to submit and asked to move within the Anxi protectorate.

sentences.zh: 太子更名紹。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent was renamed Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent was given the new name Shao.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳，改修東都明堂。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the Bright Hall of the eastern capital was rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the eastern capital's Bright Hall was rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，上幸驪山温泉；

translations.literal: On bingxu the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛-{丑}-，還宮。

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, on xinchou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on xinchou, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，明堂成。

translations.literal: On jiachen the Bright Hall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Bright Hall was finished.

sentences.zh: 劍南節度使張宥，文吏不習軍旅，悉以軍政委團練副使章仇兼瓊。

translations.literal: Jiannan military governor Zhang You, a civil official unversed in military affairs, entrusted all military matters to training vice-commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan military governor Zhang You, a clerk who knew nothing of war, handed all military affairs to training vice-commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong.

sentences.zh: 兼瓊入奏事，盛言安戎城可取，上悅之。

translations.literal: Jianqiong entered court to report affairs and spoke at length that Anrong city could be taken; the Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong came to court and urged that Anrong city could be seized; the Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以宥爲光祿卿。

translations.literal: On dingsi You was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Zhang You was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以兼瓊爲劍南節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jianqiong was made military governor of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jianqiong was appointed military governor of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 初，睿宗喪既除，祫-{於}-太廟；

translations.literal: At first, after the mourning for Ruizong had ended, a collective sacrifice was held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, once mourning for Ruizong had ended, a collective sacrifice was held in the Imperial Ancestral Temple;

sentences.zh: 自是三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: from then on there was a collective sacrifice every three years and a greater di sacrifice every five years.
translations.idiomatic: thereafter a collective sacrifice came every three years and a greater di sacrifice every five.

sentences.zh: 是歳，夏既禘，冬又當祫。

translations.literal: That year, after the di sacrifice in summer, winter again called for the collective sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: That year the di sacrifice had already been held in summer, yet winter again required the collective sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太常議以爲祭數則瀆，請停今年祫祭，自是通計五年一祫、一禘；

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices judged that too many sacrifices would be irreverent and requested that this year's collective sacrifice be suspended; from then on both would be reckoned together, one collective sacrifice and one di sacrifice every five years;
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that too many rites would profane the spirits and asked to skip this year's collective sacrifice; henceforth both would be counted together—one collective sacrifice and one di sacrifice every five years;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，上幸驪山温泉；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 庚子，還宮。

translations.literal: on gengzi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on gengzi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 二月，荊州長史張九齡卒。

translations.literal: In the second month Zhang Jiuling, chief administrator of Jingzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Zhang Jiuling, chief administrator of Jingzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 上雖以九齡忤旨逐之，然終愛重其人，毎宰相-{薦}-士，輒問曰：「風度得如九齡不？

translations.literal: Although the Emperor had banished Jiuling for opposing his will, he still cherished the man to the end; whenever a chancellor recommended an official, he would ask: "Does his bearing match Jiuling's?
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor had driven Jiuling away for crossing him, he still esteemed the man; whenever a chancellor recommended an official he would ask, "Does his bearing match Jiuling's?

sentences.zh: 三月，丁亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day dinghai, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day dinghai, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 章仇兼瓊潛與安戎城中吐蕃翟都局及維州別駕董承晏結謀，使局開門引内唐兵，盡殺吐蕃將卒，使監察-{御}-史許遠將兵守之。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiu Jianqiong secretly plotted with the Tibetan Zhai Duju in Anrong city and Weizhou vice-prefect Dong Chengyan, making Duju open the gates to admit Tang troops, killing all Tibetan officers and soldiers, and sent investigating censor Xu Yuan to lead troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Jianqiong secretly allied with the Tibetan Zhai Duju inside Anrong city and Weizhou vice-prefect Dong Chengyan; Duju opened the gates to Tang troops, who slaughtered every Tibetan officer and soldier, and Jianqiong put investigating censor Xu Yuan in command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 遠，敬宗之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan was a great-grandson of Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was a great-grandson of Emperor Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，蓋嘉運入獻捷。

translations.literal: On jiayin Gai Jiayun entered court to present news of victory.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Gai Jiayun came to court to report his victory.

sentences.zh: 上赦吐火仙罪，以爲左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned Tuhuoxian's crimes and made him general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned Tuhuoxian and appointed him general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉運請立阿史那懷道之子昕爲十姓可汗；

translations.literal: Jiayun requested that Ashina Huaidao's son Xin be established as qaghan of the Ten Surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun asked that Ashina Huaidao's son Xin be made qaghan of the Ten Surnames;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛未，以昕妻李氏爲交河公主。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei Xin's wife, Lady Li, was made Princess of Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei Xin's wife Lady Li was made Princess of Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 六月，吐蕃圍安戎城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Tibet besieged Anrong city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Tibet laid siege to Anrong city.

sentences.zh: 上嘉蓋嘉運之功，以爲河西、隴右節度使，使之經略吐蕃。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired Gai Jiayun's achievements and made him military governor of Hexi and Longyou, charging him to manage affairs against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised Gai Jiayun's victories and made him military governor of Hexi and Longyou to direct operations against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 嘉運恃恩流連，不時-{發}-。

translations.literal: Jiayun, relying on favor, lingered on and did not set out in season.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun, secure in imperial favor, lingered at court and did not depart on time.

sentences.zh: 左丞相裴耀卿上疎，以爲：「臣近與嘉運同班，觀其舉措，誠勇烈有-{餘}-，然言氣矜誇，恐難成事。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Pei Yaojing submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has recently been on the same roster as Jiayun and observed his conduct: he is indeed more than brave and fierce, yet his words and bearing are arrogant and boastful; I fear he will be hard put to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Pei Yaojing memorialized the throne: "I have lately served on the same roster as Jiayun and watched him closely: he is brave enough, yet his speech is proud and boastful; I fear he will not succeed.

sentences.zh: 昔莫敖忸-{於}-蒲騷之役，卒喪楚師；

translations.literal: In old times the Mo'ao was heedless at the battle of Pusao and in the end lost the Chu army;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Mo'ao underrated his foe at Pusao and lost the entire Chu army;

sentences.zh: 今嘉運有驕敵之色，臣竊憂之。

translations.literal: now Jiayun shows the color of one who despises the enemy; your servant privately worries.
translations.idiomatic: now Jiayun wears the look of a man who scorns his foe; I am privately alarmed.

sentences.zh: 況防秋非遠，未言-{發}-日，若臨事始去，則吏卒尚未相識，何以-{制}-敵！

translations.literal: Moreover the autumn defense is not far off, and no day of departure has been named; if he only leaves when the crisis comes, then officers and soldiers will not yet know one another—how can he control the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover autumn defense is near, yet no departure date has been set; if he waits until the crisis to leave, officers and men will still be strangers to one another—how then can he face the enemy!

sentences.zh: 且將軍受命，鑿凶門而出；

translations.literal: Besides, when a general receives his commission he bores through the Gate of Omens and marches forth;
translations.idiomatic: When a general takes command he is supposed to bore through the Gate of Omens and march;

sentences.zh: 今乃酣宴朝夕，殆非憂國愛人之心。

translations.literal: now he feasts and drinks morning and evening—hardly the heart of one who worries for the state and loves his men.
translations.idiomatic: yet now he feasts day and night—hardly the mind of a man who cares for the realm and his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 若不可改易，宜速遣進塗，仍乞聖恩嚴加訓勵。

translations.literal: If this cannot be changed, he should quickly be sent on the road, and I still beg your sage grace to admonish and encourage him sternly.
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot mend his ways, send him on the road at once, and I beg Your Majesty to admonish him sharply.

sentences.zh: 」上乃趣嘉運行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon urged Jiayun to depart.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then pressed Jiayun to march.

sentences.zh: 已而嘉運竟無功。

translations.literal: Before long Jiayun in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Jiayun accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，甲戌，幽州奏破奚、契丹。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on jiaxu, Youzhou reported defeating the Xi and Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on jiaxu, Youzhou reported victories over the Xi and Khitan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，上幸驪山温泉；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，還宮。

translations.literal: on xinsi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on xinsi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇安戎城及維州；

translations.literal: Tibet raided Anrong city and Weizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Tibet attacked Anrong city and Weizhou;

sentences.zh: -{發}-關中強騎救之，吐蕃引去。

translations.literal: strong cavalry from Guanzhong were dispatched to rescue them, and Tibet withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: the court sent strong Guanzhong cavalry to the rescue, and Tibet withdrew.

sentences.zh: 更命安戎城曰平戎。

translations.literal: Anrong city was renamed Pingrong.
translations.idiomatic: Anrong city was renamed Pingrong, "Pacify the Barbarians."

sentences.zh: 十一月，罷牛仙客朔方、河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Niu Xianke was removed as military governor of Shuofang and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Niu Xianke was relieved of the Shuofang and Hedong commands.

sentences.zh: 突騎施莫賀達-{干}-聞阿史那昕爲可汗，怒曰：「首誅蘇祿，我之謀也；

translations.literal: The Turgesh Mohedagan, hearing that Ashina Xin had been made qaghan, said in anger: "The first to plot the execution of Sulu was I;
translations.idiomatic: Turgesh leader Mohedagan, learning that Ashina Xin had been made qaghan, raged: "I was first to plot Sulu's death;

sentences.zh: 今立史昕，何以賞我？

translations.literal: now they establish Shi Xin—how is this to reward me?
translations.idiomatic: now you set up Shi Xin—what reward is that for me?

sentences.zh: 」遂帥諸部叛。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led the various tribes in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led the tribes in revolt.

sentences.zh: 上乃立莫賀達-{干}-爲可汗，使統突騎施之衆，命蓋嘉運招諭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then established Mohedagan as qaghan, making him rule the Turgesh multitude, and ordered Gai Jiayun to summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then made Mohedagan qaghan over the Turgesh and ordered Gai Jiayun to win him back.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，莫賀達-{干}-降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Mohedagan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Mohedagan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 金城公主薨；

translations.literal: Princess Jincheng died;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jincheng died;

sentences.zh: 吐蕃告喪，且請和，上不許。

translations.literal: Tibet announced the mourning and also requested peace; the Emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet announced her death and asked for peace; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 是歳，天下縣千五百七十三，戸八百四十一萬二千八百七十一，口四千八百一十四萬三千六百九。

translations.literal: That year throughout the realm there were 1,573 counties, 8,412,871 households, and 48,143,609 persons.
translations.idiomatic: That year the realm had 1,573 counties, 8,412,871 households, and 48,143,609 people.

sentences.zh: 西京、東都米斛直錢不滿二百，絹匹亦如之。

translations.literal: In the western capital and eastern capital a hu of rice cost less than two hundred cash, and a bolt of silk was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an and Luoyang a hu of rice cost under two hundred cash, and silk by the bolt the same.

sentences.zh: 海内富安，行者雖萬-{里}-不持寸兵。

translations.literal: Within the seas there was wealth and peace; travelers though ten thousand li distant carried not an inch of weapon.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was rich and at peace; a traveler might go ten thousand li without bearing a weapon.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，上幸驪山温泉。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，-{制}-：「承前諸州饑饉，皆待奏報，然始開倉賑給。

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict [said]: "Formerly, when various prefectures suffered famine, all waited for memorials to be reported before granaries were opened for relief.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou an edict declared: "In the past, when prefectures suffered famine, relief waited on memorials reaching the throne before granaries opened.

sentences.zh: 道路悠遠，何救懸絶！

translations.literal: The roads are long and far—how can one save those hanging by a thread!
translations.idiomatic: The roads are long—how can that save men at the edge of death!

sentences.zh: 自今委州縣長官與採訪使量事給訖奏聞。

translations.literal: From now on let prefectural and county chiefs together with the investigation commissioners measure affairs, distribute relief, and then memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth let prefectural and county officials and the investigation commissioners dispense relief as needed and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 庚子，上還宮。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 上夢玄元皇帝告-{云}-：「吾有像在京城西南百-{餘}--{里}-，汝遣人求之，吾當與汝興慶宮相見。

translations.literal: The Emperor dreamed that the Supreme Emperor of the Dark Origin told him: "I have an image more than a hundred li southwest of the capital; send men to seek it, and I shall meet you at Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dreamed that the Supreme Emperor of the Dark Origin said to him: "My image lies more than a hundred li southwest of the capital; send men to find it, and I shall meet you at Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 」上遣使求得之-{於}-盩厔樓觀山間。

translations.literal: " The Emperor sent envoys, who found it among the mountains of the Louguan observatory in Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent envoys, who found it in the Louguan hills of Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 夏，閏四月，迎置興慶宮。

translations.literal: In summer, in the intercalary fourth month, it was welcomed and installed at Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the intercalary fourth month, the image was brought to Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 五月，命畫玄元眞容，分置諸州開元觀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he ordered the true likeness of the Dark Origin to be painted and distributed to the Kaiyuan abbeys of the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he ordered portraits of the Dark Origin painted and sent to the Kaiyuan abbeys in every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月，吐蕃四十萬衆入寇，至安仁軍，渾崖峰騎將臧希液帥衆五千撃破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month four hundred thousand Tibetans invaded, reaching Anren Army; Zang Xiye, cavalry commander of Hunyafeng, led five thousand men and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month four hundred thousand Tibetans invaded as far as Anren Army; cavalry commander Zang Xiye of Hunyafeng led five thousand men and routed them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅，突厥遣使來告登利可汗之喪。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, the Turks sent envoys to announce the mourning for Qaghan Dengli.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, the Turks sent envoys to announce Qaghan Dengli's death.

sentences.zh: 初，登利從叔二人，分典兵馬，號左、右殺。

translations.literal: At first Dengli had two younger uncles who separately commanded troops and horses, styled the Left and Right Shas.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dengli had two younger uncles who each commanded troops, known as the Left and Right Shas.

sentences.zh: 登利患兩殺之專，與其母謀，誘右殺，斬之，自將其衆。

translations.literal: Dengli feared the monopoly of the two Shas; with his mother he plotted, lured the Right Sha, beheaded him, and himself led his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dengli resented the Shas' power; with his mother he lured the Right Sha, killed him, and took command of his men.

sentences.zh: 左殺判闕特勒兵攻登利，殺之，立毘伽可汗之子爲可汗；

translations.literal: The Left Sha Pankue Tegri led troops to attack Dengli, killed him, and established a son of Qaghan Pijia as qaghan;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Sha Pankue led his army against Dengli, killed him, and set up a son of Qaghan Pijia as qaghan;

sentences.zh: 俄爲骨咄-{葉}-護所殺，更立其弟；

translations.literal: before long he was killed by the yabghu Kutlug Yabghu, who established his younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: soon Kutlug Yabghu killed him and set up his younger brother;

sentences.zh: 尋又殺之，骨咄-{葉}-護自立爲可汗。

translations.literal: before long he killed him too, and Kutlug Yabghu established himself as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: then killed him as well and made himself qaghan.

sentences.zh: 上以突厥内亂，癸酉，命左羽林將軍孫老奴招諭回紇、葛邏祿、拔悉密等部落。
