translations.literal: Because the Turks were in internal disorder, on guiyou the Emperor ordered Left Forest Guard general Sun Laonu to summon and instruct the Uyghur, Qarluq, Basmyl, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Turks in civil war, on guiyou the Emperor ordered Left Forest Guard general Sun Laonu to win over the Uyghurs, Qarluqs, Basmyls, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，東都洛水溢，溺死者千-{餘}-人。

translations.literal: On yihai the Luo River at the eastern capital overflowed; more than a thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Luo River flooded Luoyang; more than a thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 平盧兵馬使安祿山，傾巧，善事人，人多譽之。

translations.literal: Pinglu army horse commander An Lushan was clever and artful, skilled at pleasing people, and many praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu army horse commander An Lushan was cunning, knew how to please men, and many praised him.

sentences.zh: 上左右至平盧者，祿山皆厚賂之，由是上益以爲賢。

translations.literal: Those about the Emperor who came to Pinglu—Lushan bribed them all heavily; thereby the Emperor increasingly regarded him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Every courtier who visited Pinglu Lushan paid lavishly; the Emperor came to think him ever more able.

sentences.zh: -{御}-史中丞張利貞爲河北採訪使，至平盧。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Lizhen was investigation commissioner of Hebei and came to Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Lizhen, Hebei investigation commissioner, visited Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 祿山-{曲}-事利貞，乃至左右皆有賂。

translations.literal: Lushan attended to Lizhen with every courtesy, even to the point that those about him all received bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan waited on Lizhen with every courtesy; even Lizhen's attendants were bribed.

sentences.zh: 利貞入奏，盛稱祿山之美。

translations.literal: Lizhen entered court to report and spoke at length in praise of Lushan's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen returned to court and praised Lushan at length.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙未，以祿山爲營州都督，充平盧軍使，兩蕃、勃海、黑水四府經略使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yiwei, Lushan was made protector of Yingzhou, acting Pinglu army commander, and commissioner over the four circuits of the Two Fan, Bohai, and Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiwei, Lushan was made protector of Yingzhou, Pinglu army commander, and commissioner over the Two Fan, Bohai, and Heishui circuits.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙申，上幸驪山温泉。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingshen, the Emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingshen, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，分北庭、安西爲二節度。

translations.literal: On renyin Beiting and Anxi were divided into two military governorships.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Beiting and Anxi were split into two separate commands.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚戌，司空邠王守禮薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, Minister of Works Prince Bin Shouli died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, Minister of Works Prince Bin Shouli died.

sentences.zh: 守禮庸鄙無-{才}-識，毎天將雨及霽，守禮必先言之，已而皆驗。

translations.literal: Shouli was mediocre, vulgar, and without talent or insight; whenever rain was about to fall or the sky was about to clear, Shouli always spoke of it first, and afterward it always proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Shouli was mediocre and dull-witted; yet whenever rain was coming or the sky was about to clear, he always announced it first—and he was invariably right.

sentences.zh: 岐、薛諸王言-{於}-上曰：「邠兄有-{術}-。

translations.literal: The princes of Qi and Xue said to the Emperor: "Our elder brother of Bin has arts.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Qi and Xue told the Emperor: "Our elder brother of Bin has supernatural skill.

sentences.zh: 」上問其故，對曰：「臣無-{術}-。

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Your servant has no arts.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor asked why, he answered: "I have no such arts.

sentences.zh: 則天時以章懷之故，幽閉宮中十-{餘}-年，歳賜敕杖者數四，背瘢甚厚，將雨則沉悶，將霽則輕爽，臣以此知之耳。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, because of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, I was shut up in the palace for more than ten years; several times each year I was granted imperial caning, and the scars on my back grew very thick—when rain was coming I felt heavy oppression, and when the sky was about to clear I felt light relief; your servant knew it only from this.
translations.idiomatic: In Empress Wu's time, because of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, I was confined in the palace for more than ten years and was caned by imperial order several times a year until my back was thick with scars. When rain was coming I felt heavy and oppressed; when the sky was about to clear I felt light and refreshed. I knew the weather only from that.

sentences.zh: 」因流涕沾襟；

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears streamed down and soaked his robe;
translations.idiomatic: " He wept until his robe was soaked;

sentences.zh: 上亦爲之慘然。

translations.literal: the Emperor too was deeply moved on his account.
translations.idiomatic: and the Emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上還宮。

translations.literal: On xinyou the Emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛未，太尉-{寧}-王憲薨。

translations.literal: On xinwei Grand Preceptor Prince Ning Li Xian died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Grand Preceptor Prince Ning Li Xian died.

sentences.zh: 上哀惋特甚，曰：「天下，兄之天下也；

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved with exceptional sorrow and said: "The realm was my elder brother's realm;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved with exceptional sorrow and said: "The realm was my brother's realm;

sentences.zh: 兄固讓-{於}-我，爲唐太伯，常名不足以處之。

translations.literal: my elder brother firmly yielded it to me and was the Taibo of Tang—an ordinary title is not enough to do him justice.
translations.idiomatic: my brother firmly yielded it to me and was the Taibo of Tang—no ordinary title could do him justice.

sentences.zh: 」乃謚曰讓皇帝。

translations.literal: " He thereupon gave the posthumous title Emperor Rang.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon gave him the posthumous title Emperor Rang.

sentences.zh: 其子汝陽王璡，上表追述先-{志}-謙-{沖}-，不敢當帝號；

translations.literal: His son, Prince of Ruyang Li Jin, memorialized recalling his father's humble and yielding intent and declaring that he dared not accept the title of emperor;
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince of Ruyang Li Jin, memorialized that his father had been humble and yielding in life and that the family dared not accept an imperial title;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 敛日，内出服，以手書致-{於}-靈座，書稱「隆基白」；

translations.literal: On the day the body was laid in state the Emperor sent mourning garments from within the palace and with his own hand wrote to the spirit seat, signing himself "Bai from Longji";
translations.idiomatic: On the day the body was laid in state he sent mourning garments from within the palace and wrote in his own hand to the spirit seat, signing himself "Respectfully, Longji";

sentences.zh: 又名其墓曰惠陵，追謚其妃元氏曰恭皇-{后}-，附葬焉。

translations.literal: he also named the tomb Huiling, posthumously titled his consort Lady Yuan as Empress Gong, and had her buried there with him.
translations.idiomatic: he named the tomb Huiling, posthumously titled his consort Lady Yuan as Empress Gong, and had her buried there with him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙巳，吐蕃屠達化縣，陷石堡城，蓋嘉運不能-{御}-。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yisi, Tibet massacred Dahua County, captured Shibao Fortress, and Gai Jiayun could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yisi, Tibet massacred Dahua County, captured Shibao Fortress, and Gai Jiayun could not drive them off.
